input: The Odrysian Kingdom was a union of Thracian tribes under the kings of the powerful Odrysian tribe centered around the region of Thrace. Various parts of Thrace were under Macedonian rule under Philip II of Macedon, Alexander the Great, Lysimachus, Ptolemy II, and Philip V but were also often ruled by their own kings. The Thracians and Agrianes were widely used by Alexander as peltasts and light cavalry, forming about one fifth of his army. The Diadochi also used Thracian mercenaries in their armies and they were also used as colonists. The Odrysians used Greek as the language of administration and of the nobility. The nobility also adopted Greek fashions in dress, ornament and military equipment, spreading it to the other tribes. Thracian kings were among the first to be Hellenized.
rewrite: Centered in Thrace, the Odrysian Kingdom united various Thracian tribes under the rule of the powerful Odrysians. While Macedonian rulers like Philip II, Alexander the Great, and others controlled parts of Thrace, the region was also frequently governed by its own native kings. Alexander the Great extensively employed Thracians and Agrianes as peltasts and light cavalry, which constituted roughly a fifth of his forces. Subsequent Diadochi armies also relied on Thracian mercenaries and utilized them as colonists. Within the Odrysian realm, Greek served as the administrative and noble language. The nobility adopted Greek styles in clothing, ornamentation, and military gear, disseminating these customs to other tribes. Consequently, Thracian kings were some of the earliest to become Hellenized.

input: Madonna's music has been the subject of much analysis and scrutiny. Robert M. Grant, author of Contemporary Strategy Analysis (2005), commented that what has brought Madonna success is "certainly not outstanding natural talent. As a vocalist, musician, dancer, songwriter, or actress, Madonna's talents seem modest." He asserts Madonna's success is in relying on the talents of others, and that her personal relationships have served as cornerstones to the numerous reinventions in the longevity of her career. Madonna's approach was far from the music industry wisdom of "Find a winning formula and stick to it." Her musical career has been a continuous experimentation with new musical ideas and new images and a constant quest for new heights of fame and acclaim. Grant concluded that "having established herself as the queen of popular music, Madonna did not stop there, but continued re-inventing." Musicologist Susan McClary wrote that "Madonna's art itself repeatedly deconstructs the traditional notion of the unified subject with finite ego boundaries. Her pieces explore various ways of constituting identities that refuse stability, that remain fluid, that resist definition."
rewrite: Madonna’s musical career has defied conventional industry wisdom, which often advises finding a winning formula and adhering to it. Instead, her path has been marked by continuous experimentation with new musical ideas and images, as well as a persistent drive for greater fame and acclaim. According to Robert M. Grant, author of *Contemporary Strategy Analysis* (2005), Madonna’s success stems not from “outstanding natural talent”—her abilities as a vocalist, musician, dancer, songwriter, or actress being, in his view, modest—but from her reliance on the talents of others. He notes that her personal relationships have been foundational to the numerous reinventions that have characterized her enduring career. Grant observes that even after establishing herself as the queen of popular music, Madonna never ceased reinventing herself. Musicologist Susan McClary further analyzes Madonna’s work, writing that her art consistently deconstructs the traditional concept of a unified self with fixed ego boundaries. McClary explains that Madonna’s pieces investigate ways of forming identities that reject stability, embrace fluidity, and resist clear definition.

input: Following the death of Pope Pius XII on 9 October 1958, Roncalli watched the live funeral on his last full day in Venice on 11 October. His journal was specifically concerned with the funeral and the abused state of the late pontiff's corpse. Roncalli left Venice for the conclave in Rome well aware that he was papabile,[b] and after eleven ballots, was elected to succeed the late Pius XII, so it came as no surprise to him, though he had arrived at the Vatican with a return train ticket to Venice.[citation needed]
rewrite: On his final day in Venice, October 11, 1958, Roncalli viewed the live funeral of Pope Pius XII, who had died two days prior. His journal focused on the rites and the deteriorated condition of the former pontiff's body. Traveling to Rome for the conclave, Roncalli was conscious of being a papal candidate. His election after eleven ballots, while unsurprising to him, contrasted with his practical preparations—he had brought a return train ticket to Venice.

input: When granting assent by commission, the sovereign authorises three or more (normally five) lords who are Privy Counsellors to grant assent in his or her name. The Lords Commissioners, as the monarch's representatives are known, wear scarlet parliamentary robes and sit on a bench between the throne and the Woolsack. The Lords Reading Clerk reads the commission aloud; the senior commissioner then states, "My Lords, in obedience to Her Majesty's Commands, and by virtue of the Commission which has been now read, We do declare and notify to you, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in Parliament assembled, that Her Majesty has given Her Royal Assent to the several Acts in the Commission mentioned."
rewrite: In the process of granting assent by commission, the sovereign delegates authority to three or more Privy Counsellors, typically five lords, to act in his or her name. These representatives, known as the Lords Commissioners, are clad in scarlet parliamentary robes and occupy a bench situated between the throne and the Woolsack. The Lords Reading Clerk proceeds to read the commission aloud. Following this, the senior commissioner declares: "My Lords, in obedience to Her Majesty's Commands, and by virtue of the Commission which has been now read, We do declare and notify to you, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal and Commons in Parliament assembled, that Her Majesty has given Her Royal Assent to the several Acts in the Commission mentioned."

input: Approximately 26,000 citizen soldiers, sailors, and airmen and women, trained to the level of and interchangeable with their Regular Force counterparts, and posted to CAF operations or duties on a casual or ongoing basis, make up the Primary Reserve. This group is represented, though not commanded, at NDHQ by the Chief of Reserves and Cadets, who is usually a major general or rear admiral, and is divided into four components that are each operationally and administratively responsible to its corresponding environmental command in the Regular Force – the Naval Reserve (NAVRES), Land Force Reserve (LFR), and Air Reserve (AIRRES) – in addition to one force that does not fall under an environmental command, the Health Services Reserve under the Canadian Forces Health Services Group.
rewrite: The Primary Reserve consists of roughly 26,000 citizen soldiers, sailors, and air personnel. These members are trained to the same standard as the Regular Force and can serve in their roles, being posted to Canadian Armed Forces operations either casually or on an ongoing basis. Though not under their command, this group is represented at National Defence Headquarters by the Chief of Reserves and Cadets, typically a major general or rear admiral. It is divided into four components. Three of these—the Naval Reserve (NAVRES), Land Force Reserve (LFR), and Air Reserve (AIRRES)—are each operationally and administratively aligned with their respective environmental command in the Regular Force. The fourth is the Health Services Reserve, which falls under the Canadian Forces Health Services Group rather than an environmental command.

input: In the early Western Han, a wealthy salt or iron industrialist, whether a semi-autonomous king or wealthy merchant, could boast funds that rivaled the imperial treasury and amass a peasant workforce of over a thousand. This kept many peasants away from their farms and denied the government a significant portion of its land tax revenue. To eliminate the influence of such private entrepreneurs, Emperor Wu nationalized the salt and iron industries in 117 BC and allowed many of the former industrialists to become officials administering the monopolies. By Eastern Han times, the central government monopolies were repealed in favor of production by commandery and county administrations, as well as private businessmen.
rewrite: During the early Western Han period, influential salt or iron industrialists—whether semi-autonomous kings or wealthy merchants—could command resources matching the imperial treasury and employ peasant workforces exceeding a thousand. This drew numerous peasants from agriculture, depriving the state of substantial land tax income. To curb the power of these private entrepreneurs, Emperor Wu nationalized the salt and iron trades in 117 BC, even appointing many former industrialists as officials to oversee the new monopolies. By the Eastern Han era, these central government monopolies were abolished, shifting production to commandery and county administrations alongside private businessmen.

input: The topography of the state is roughly defined by the Continental Divide, which splits much of the state into distinct eastern and western regions. Most of Montana's 100 or more named mountain ranges are concentrated in the western half of the state, most of which is geologically and geographically part of the Northern Rocky Mountains. The Absaroka and Beartooth ranges in the south-central part of the state are technically part of the Central Rocky Mountains. The Rocky Mountain Front is a significant feature in the north-central portion of the state, and there are a number of isolated island ranges that interrupt the prairie landscape common in the central and eastern parts of the state. About 60 percent of the state is prairie, part of the northern Great Plains.
rewrite: Montana’s landscape is broadly shaped by the Continental Divide, creating distinct eastern and western areas. The majority of the state’s over 100 named mountain ranges lie in the west, largely within the Northern Rocky Mountains. Exceptions include the Absaroka and Beartooth ranges in the south-central region, which belong to the Central Rocky Mountains. Significant features also include the Rocky Mountain Front in the north-central portion and isolated island ranges that rise from the prairies common to the central and eastern parts. Roughly 60 percent of Montana consists of prairie, forming a section of the northern Great Plains.

input: Birds have evolved a variety of mating behaviors, with the peacock tail being perhaps the most famous example of sexual selection and the Fisherian runaway. Commonly occurring sexual dimorphisms such as size and color differences are energetically costly attributes that signal competitive breeding situations. Many types of avian sexual selection have been identified; intersexual selection, also known as female choice; and intrasexual competition, where individuals of the more abundant sex compete with each other for the privilege to mate. Sexually selected traits often evolve to become more pronounced in competitive breeding situations until the trait begins to limit the individual’s fitness. Conflicts between an individual fitness and signaling adaptations ensure that sexually selected ornaments such as plumage coloration and courtship behavior are "honest" traits. Signals must be costly to ensure that only good-quality individuals can present these exaggerated sexual ornaments and behaviors.
rewrite: The peacock’s elaborate tail stands as a famous illustration of sexual selection and the Fisherian runaway process, highlighting the diverse mating behaviors birds have evolved. In competitive breeding scenarios, energetically costly traits like size and color differences—common sexual dimorphisms—serve as signals. Avian sexual selection takes multiple forms, including intersexual selection (female choice) and intrasexual competition, where members of the more abundant sex vie for mating opportunities. These sexually selected traits often become increasingly pronounced, sometimes to the point of limiting an individual’s fitness. To remain “honest” signals, ornaments like vivid plumage and complex courtship displays must involve significant cost, ensuring only high-quality individuals can sustain such exaggerated features and behaviors. This tension between individual fitness and signaling adaptations upholds the reliability of these displays.

input: Great Britain: The torch relay leg held in London, the host city of the 2012 Summer Olympics, on April 6 began at Wembley Stadium, passed through the City of London, and eventually ended at O2 Arena in the eastern part of the city. The 48 km (30 mi) leg took a total of seven and a half hours to complete, and attracted protests by pro-Tibetan independence and pro-Human Rights supporters, prompting changes to the planned route and an unscheduled move onto a bus, which was then briefly halted by protestors. Home Secretary Jacqui Smith has officially complained to Beijing Organising Committee about the conduct of the tracksuit-clad Chinese security guards. The Chinese officials, seen manhandling protesters, were described by both the London Mayor Ken Livingstone and Lord Coe, chairman of the London Olympic Committee as "thugs". A Metropolitan police briefing paper revealed that security for the torch relay cost £750,000 and the participation of the Chinese security team had been agreed in advance, despite the Mayor stating, "We did not know beforehand these thugs were from the security services. Had I known so, we would have said no."
rewrite: On April 6, the Olympic torch relay traveled through London, the host city for the 2012 Summer Games. Beginning at Wembley Stadium, the procession moved through the City of London before concluding at the O2 Arena in the city's east. This 48 km (30 mi) segment lasted seven and a half hours. Throughout the event, pro-Tibetan independence and human rights activists staged protests, which forced alterations to the planned route. At one point, the relay was moved onto a bus, only for that bus to be briefly stopped by demonstrators. London Mayor Ken Livingstone and Lord Coe, chairman of the London Olympic Committee, both labeled the tracksuit-clad Chinese security officials seen manhandling protesters as "thugs." Home Secretary Jacqui Smith lodged an official complaint with the Beijing Organising Committee regarding their conduct. A Metropolitan Police briefing disclosed that security for the relay cost £750,000 and that the involvement of the Chinese security team had been pre-approved. This was despite Mayor Livingstone's later assertion: "We did not know beforehand these thugs were from the security services. Had I known so, we would have said no."

input: The government of India is based on a tiered system, in which the Constitution of India delineates the subjects on which each tier of government has executive powers. The Constitution originally provided for a two-tier system of government, the Union Government (also known as the Central Government), representing the Union of India, and the State governments. Later, a third tier was added in the form of Panchayats and Municipalities. In the current arrangement, The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution delimits the subjects of each level of governmental jurisdiction, dividing them into three lists:
rewrite: India's governmental structure operates on a tiered framework, with executive powers for each level defined by the Constitution. Initially, this system comprised two tiers: the Union (or Central) Government and the State governments. A third tier, consisting of Panchayats and Municipalities, was subsequently introduced. Presently, the distribution of jurisdictional subjects among these levels is detailed in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, which organizes them into three distinct lists.

input: In an effort to demonstrate peaceful intentions toward Germany, on 13 April 1941, the Soviets signed a neutrality pact with Axis power Japan. While Stalin had little faith in Japan's commitment to neutrality, he felt that the pact was important for its political symbolism, to reinforce a public affection for Germany. Stalin felt that there was a growing split in German circles about whether Germany should initiate a war with the Soviet Union. Stalin did not know that Hitler had been secretly discussing an invasion of the Soviet Union since summer 1940, and that Hitler had ordered his military in late 1940 to prepare for war in the east regardless of the parties' talks of a potential Soviet entry as a fourth Axis Power.
rewrite: On 13 April 1941, the Soviet Union signed a neutrality pact with Japan, an Axis power, aiming to show peaceful intentions toward Germany. Stalin viewed the pact as politically symbolic, crucial for fostering public goodwill toward Germany, despite his own skepticism about Japan's dedication to neutrality. He perceived a growing division within German leadership regarding the prospect of launching a war against the Soviets. Unbeknownst to Stalin, Hitler had been secretly planning an invasion since summer 1940. By late 1940, Hitler had already commanded his military to prepare for an eastern war, even as discussions about potentially bringing the Soviet Union into the Axis as a fourth member were still occurring.

input: Ottoman Turkish was the official language of the Empire. It was an Oghuz Turkic language highly influenced by Persian and Arabic. The Ottomans had several influential languages: Turkish, spoken by the majority of the people in Anatolia and by the majority of Muslims of the Balkans except in Albania and Bosnia; Persian, only spoken by the educated; Arabic, spoken mainly in Arabia, North Africa, Iraq, Kuwait, the Levant and parts of the Horn of Africa; and Somali throughout the Horn of Africa. In the last two centuries, usage of these became limited, though, and specific: Persian served mainly as a literary language for the educated, while Arabic was used for religious rites.
rewrite: As the official language of the Ottoman Empire, Ottoman Turkish was an Oghuz Turkic language heavily influenced by Persian and Arabic. The empire itself utilized several key languages. Turkish was spoken by most people in Anatolia and by the majority of Balkan Muslims, except in Albania and Bosnia. Arabic was used primarily in Arabia, North Africa, Iraq, Kuwait, the Levant, and parts of the Horn of Africa, alongside Somali throughout that region. Persian was chiefly spoken by the educated class. Over the final two centuries, their usage became more limited and specialized: Persian functioned mainly as a literary language, while Arabic was reserved for religious rites.

input: In his book, Humanism (1997), Tony Davies calls these critics "humanist anti-humanists". Critics of antihumanism, most notably Jürgen Habermas, counter that while antihumanists may highlight humanism's failure to fulfil its emancipatory ideal, they do not offer an alternative emancipatory project of their own. Others, like the German philosopher Heidegger considered themselves humanists on the model of the ancient Greeks, but thought humanism applied only to the German "race" and specifically to the Nazis and thus, in Davies' words, were anti-humanist humanists. Such a reading of Heidegger's thought is itself deeply controversial; Heidegger includes his own views and critique of Humanism in Letter On Humanism. Davies acknowledges that after the horrific experiences of the wars of the 20th century "it should no longer be possible to formulate phrases like 'the destiny of man' or the 'triumph of human reason' without an instant consciousness of the folly and brutality they drag behind them". For "it is almost impossible to think of a crime that has not been committed in the name of human reason". Yet, he continues, "it would be unwise to simply abandon the ground occupied by the historical humanisms. For one thing humanism remains on many occasions the only available alternative to bigotry and persecution. The freedom to speak and write, to organise and campaign in defence of individual or collective interests, to protest and disobey: all these can only be articulated in humanist terms."
rewrite:
In his 1997 work *Humanism*, Tony Davies labels certain thinkers as "humanist anti-humanists." Among critics of antihumanism, Jürgen Habermas stands out, arguing that while antihumanists effectively expose humanism's failure to achieve its liberating goals, they fail to propose their own project for emancipation. The terrain becomes more complex with figures like the German philosopher Heidegger. Heidegger saw himself as a humanist in the ancient Greek tradition, yet he restricted this humanism to the German "race" and the Nazis specifically, making him, in Davies' phrasing, an anti-humanist humanist. This interpretation of Heidegger is highly contested, and he personally articulated his critique in *Letter on Humanism*.

Davies recognizes that the atrocities of the 20th century's wars have rendered phrases like "the destiny of man" or the "triumph of human reason" almost unspeakable, as they immediately evoke the folly and brutality committed in their wake. It is, he notes, nearly impossible to conceive of a crime not perpetrated in the name of human reason. Nevertheless, Davies contends it would be a mistake to wholly abandon the territory held by historical humanisms. He argues that humanism often remains the sole available alternative to bigotry and persecution. Fundamental freedoms—to speak, write, organize, campaign for interests, protest, and disobey—can, he asserts, only be articulated within a humanist framework.

input: In 2006, a study by Behar et al., based on what was at that time high-resolution analysis of haplogroup K (mtDNA), suggested that about 40% of the current Ashkenazi population is descended matrilineally from just four women, or "founder lineages", that were "likely from a Hebrew/Levantine mtDNA pool" originating in the Middle East in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE. Additionally, Behar et al. suggested that the rest of Ashkenazi mtDNA is originated from ~150 women, and that most of those were also likely of Middle Eastern origin. In reference specifically to Haplogroup K, they suggested that although it is common throughout western Eurasia, "the observed global pattern of distribution renders very unlikely the possibility that the four aforementioned founder lineages entered the Ashkenazi mtDNA pool via gene flow from a European host population".
rewrite: A 2006 study by Behar et al., utilizing then high-resolution analysis of mitochondrial DNA haplogroup K, indicated that roughly 40% of the modern Ashkenazi population originates from merely four maternal founder lineages. These lineages likely belonged to a Hebrew/Levantine genetic pool from the Middle East, dating to the first and second centuries CE. The researchers further suggested the remaining Ashkenazi mitochondrial DNA stems from approximately 150 women, with most also probably of Middle Eastern origin. Regarding Haplogroup K specifically, they argued that while common across western Eurasia, its global distribution pattern makes it highly improbable that the four founder lineages were introduced through gene flow from a European host population.

input: The radio stations in San Diego include nationwide broadcaster, Clear Channel Communications; CBS Radio, Midwest Television, Lincoln Financial Media, Finest City Broadcasting, and many other smaller stations and networks. input: Extended systems of underwater caves, sinkholes and springs are found throughout the state and supply most of the water used by residents. The limestone is topped with sandy soils deposited as ancient beaches over millions of years as global sea levels rose and fell. During the last glacial period, lower sea levels and a drier climate revealed a much wider peninsula, largely savanna. The Everglades, an enormously wide, slow-flowing river encompasses the southern tip of the peninsula. Sinkhole damage claims on property in the state exceeded a total of $2 billion from 2006 through 2010.
rewrite: Across the state, extensive networks of underwater caves, sinkholes, and springs provide most of the water for residents. The limestone bedrock is covered by sandy soils, remnants of ancient beaches formed over millions of years of fluctuating sea levels. In the last glacial period, lower seas and a drier climate exposed a much broader peninsula, primarily savanna. The southern tip is covered by the Everglades, an immensely wide, slow-moving river. Notably, from 2006 to 2010, property damage claims from sinkholes in the state surpassed $2 billion total.

input: Tibet was once a strong power contemporaneous with Tang China (618–907). Until the Tibetan Empire's collapse in the 9th century, it was the Tang's major rival in dominating Inner Asia. The Yarlung rulers of Tibet also signed various peace treaties with the Tang, culminating in a treaty in 821 that fixed the borders between Tibet and China.
rewrite: During the Tang dynasty (618–907), Tibet was a powerful empire and a primary rival for control of Inner Asia. Its Yarlung rulers negotiated several peace treaties with the Tang, with a key 821 agreement establishing their mutual border. This rivalry persisted until the Tibetan Empire's collapse in the 9th century.

input: The first newspaper in Namibia was the German-language Windhoeker Anzeiger, founded 1898. Radio was introduced in 1969, TV in 1981. During German rule, the newspapers mainly reflected the living reality and the view of the white German-speaking minority. The black majority was ignored or depicted as a threat. During South African rule, the white bias continued, with mentionable influence of the Pretoria government on the "South West African" media system. Independent newspapers were seen as a menace to the existing order, critical journalists threatened.
rewrite: Namibia's inaugural newspaper, the German-language Windhoeker Anzeiger, was established in 1898, followed by radio in 1969 and television in 1981. Under German administration, the press predominantly mirrored the perspectives and daily life of the white German-speaking minority, often ignoring or portraying the Black majority as a threat. This white bias persisted during South African rule, with Pretoria exerting significant influence over the "South West African" media. Independent newspapers and critical journalists were viewed as threats to the established order.

input: Hemimetabolous insects, those with incomplete metamorphosis, change gradually by undergoing a series of molts. An insect molts when it outgrows its exoskeleton, which does not stretch and would otherwise restrict the insect's growth. The molting process begins as the insect's epidermis secretes a new epicuticle inside the old one. After this new epicuticle is secreted, the epidermis releases a mixture of enzymes that digests the endocuticle and thus detaches the old cuticle. When this stage is complete, the insect makes its body swell by taking in a large quantity of water or air, which makes the old cuticle split along predefined weaknesses where the old exocuticle was thinnest.:142
rewrite: Insects with incomplete metamorphosis, known as hemimetabolous, grow through gradual molts. Their rigid exoskeleton cannot stretch, so it must be shed to allow for growth. The process starts when the epidermis forms a new epicuticle beneath the old one. Following this, the epidermis releases digestive enzymes to break down the endocuticle, separating the old cuticle. Finally, the insect ingests substantial water or air, causing its body to expand. This pressure splits the old cuticle along its weakest points, where the exocuticle was thinnest.

input: Following the death of Grand Prince Igor in 945, his wife Olga ruled as regent in Kiev until their son Sviatoslav reached maturity (ca. 963). His decade-long reign over Rus' was marked by rapid expansion through the conquest of the Khazars of the Pontic steppe and the invasion of the Balkans. By the end of his short life, Sviatoslav carved out for himself the largest state in Europe, eventually moving his capital from Kiev to Pereyaslavets on the Danube in 969. In contrast with his mother's conversion to Christianity, Sviatoslav, like his druzhina, remained a staunch pagan. Due to his abrupt death in an ambush in 972, Sviatoslav's conquests, for the most part, were not consolidated into a functioning empire, while his failure to establish a stable succession led to a fratricidal feud among his sons, which resulted in two of his three sons being killed.
rewrite: After Grand Prince Igor died in 945, his widow Olga governed as regent in Kiev until their son Sviatoslav came of age around 963. Sviatoslav’s ten-year rule saw the rapid growth of Rus’, fueled by victories over the Khazars on the Pontic steppe and campaigns into the Balkans. By 969, he had forged the largest state in Europe, shifting his capital from Kiev to Pereyaslavets on the Danube. Unlike his mother, who embraced Christianity, Sviatoslav remained a devoted pagan, as did his druzhina warriors. His reign ended abruptly when he was ambushed and killed in 972. Most of his territorial gains were never solidified into a lasting empire, and his lack of a clear succession plan plunged his sons into a deadly feud that claimed two of their lives.

input: In December 2014, Myanmar signed an agreement to set up its first stock exchange. The Yangon Stock Exchange Joint Venture Co. Ltd will be set up with Myanma Economic Bank sharing 51 percent, Japan's Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd 30.25 percent and Japan Exchange Group 18.75 percent. The Yangon Stock Exchange (YSX) officially opened for business on Friday, March 25, 2016. First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd. (FMI) became the first stock to be traded after receiving approval for an opening price of 26,000 kyats ($22).
rewrite: Myanmar's inaugural stock exchange was established through an agreement signed in December 2014. The venture, Yangon Stock Exchange Joint Venture Co. Ltd., is owned primarily by Myanma Economic Bank (51%), with Japan's Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd. (30.25%) and Japan Exchange Group (18.75%) holding the remaining shares. Operations commenced on March 25, 2016. First Myanmar Investment Co., Ltd. (FMI) debuted as the first listed stock, trading at an approved opening price of 26,000 kyats (approximately $22).

input: The Galician road network includes autopistas and autovías connecting the major cities, as well as national and secondary roads to the rest of the municipalities. The Autovía A-6 connects A Coruña and Lugo to Madrid, entering Galicia at Pedrafita do Cebreiro. The Autovía A-52 connects O Porriño, Ourense and Benavente, and enters Galicia at A Gudiña. Two more autovías are under construction. Autovía A-8 enters Galicia on the Cantabrian coast, and ends in Baamonde (Lugo province). Autovía A-76 enters Galicia in Valdeorras; it is an upgrade of the existing N-120 to Ourense and Vigo.
rewrite: Galicia's road system features autopistas and autovías linking its major cities, alongside national and secondary roads serving other municipalities. The Autovía A-6 enters the region at Pedrafita do Cebreiro, connecting A Coruña and Lugo to Madrid. Meanwhile, the A-52 reaches Galicia at A Gudiña, joining O Porriño, Ourense, and Benavente. Two additional autovías are being built: the A-8, which arrives via the Cantabrian coast and terminates in Baamonde (Lugo), and the A-76. The A-76 enters at Valdeorras and upgrades the current N-120 route to Ourense and Vigo.

input: The TD Garden, formerly called the FleetCenter and built to replace the old, since-demolished Boston Garden, is adjoined to North Station and is the home of two major league teams: the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League and the Boston Celtics of the National Basketball Association. The arena seats 18,624 for basketball games and 17,565 for ice hockey games. The Bruins were the first American member of the National Hockey League and an Original Six franchise. The Boston Celtics were founding members of the Basketball Association of America, one of the two leagues that merged to form the NBA. The Celtics have the distinction of having won more championships than any other NBA team, with seventeen.
rewrite: Home to both the Boston Bruins (National Hockey League) and Boston Celtics (National Basketball Association), TD Garden is adjoined to North Station. This arena, seating 18,624 for basketball and 17,565 for hockey, was built to replace the old Boston Garden and was originally known as the FleetCenter. The Bruins hold a historic position as both the first American NHL member and an Original Six franchise. Meanwhile, the Celtics were founding members of the Basketball Association of America, a league that later merged to create the NBA. With seventeen titles, the Celtics have won more championships than any other NBA team.

input: Charlemagne planned to continue the Frankish tradition of dividing his kingdom between all his heirs, but was unable to do so as only one son, Louis the Pious (r. 814–840), was still alive by 813. Just before Charlemagne died in 814, he crowned Louis as his successor. Louis's reign of 26 years was marked by numerous divisions of the empire among his sons and, after 829, civil wars between various alliances of father and sons over the control of various parts of the empire. Eventually, Louis recognised his eldest son Lothair I (d. 855) as emperor and gave him Italy. Louis divided the rest of the empire between Lothair and Charles the Bald (d. 877), his youngest son. Lothair took East Francia, comprising both banks of the Rhine and eastwards, leaving Charles West Francia with the empire to the west of the Rhineland and the Alps. Louis the German (d. 876), the middle child, who had been rebellious to the last, was allowed to keep Bavaria under the suzerainty of his elder brother. The division was disputed. Pepin II of Aquitaine (d. after 864), the emperor's grandson, rebelled in a contest for Aquitaine, while Louis the German tried to annex all of East Francia. Louis the Pious died in 840, with the empire still in chaos.
rewrite: Following Frankish custom, Charlemagne intended to partition his kingdom among his heirs, yet by 813 only a single son survived: Louis the Pious, who reigned from 814 to 840. Just prior to his death in 814, Charlemagne personally crowned Louis as his successor. Louis’s 26-year rule was defined by repeated divisions of the empire among his sons and, after 829, by civil wars. These conflicts saw shifting alliances of father and sons battling for control over imperial territories. Ultimately, Louis acknowledged his eldest son, Lothair I (d. 855), as emperor and granted him Italy. The remaining empire was divided between Lothair and the youngest son, Charles the Bald (d. 877). Lothair received East Francia, encompassing lands on both sides of the Rhine and extending eastward, while Charles was given West Francia, the territories west of the Rhineland and the Alps. The middle son, the persistently rebellious Louis the German (d. 876), was permitted to retain Bavaria under his elder brother’s overlordship. This settlement was immediately contested. The emperor’s grandson, Pepin II of Aquitaine (d. after 864), rebelled in a struggle for Aquitaine, and Louis the German attempted to seize all of East Francia. When Louis the Pious died in 840, the empire remained engulfed in turmoil.

input: High neoclassicism was an international movement. Though neoclassical architecture employed the same classical vocabulary as Late Baroque architecture, it tended to emphasize its planar qualities, rather than sculptural volumes. Projections and recessions and their effects of light and shade were more flat; sculptural bas-reliefs were flatter and tended to be enframed in friezes, tablets or panels. Its clearly articulated individual features were isolated rather than interpenetrating, autonomous and complete in themselves.
rewrite: High neoclassicism emerged as an international movement. While it shared a classical vocabulary with Late Baroque architecture, it emphasized planar qualities over sculptural volumes. Features like projections and recessions produced flatter effects of light and shade. Bas-reliefs became shallower, often framed within friezes or panels. Its individual elements were clearly articulated, isolated, and autonomous, each appearing complete in itself.

input: Before creation of Warsaw Pact, fearing Germany rearmed, Czechoslovak leadership sought to create security pact with East Germany and Poland. These states protested strongly against re-militarization of West Germany. The Warsaw Pact was primarily put in place as a consequence of the rearming of West Germany inside NATO. Soviet leaders, as many European countries in both western and eastern side, feared Germany being once again a military power as a direct threat and German militarism remained a fresh memory among Soviets and Eastern Europeans. As Soviet Union had already bilateral treaties with all of its eastern satellites, the Pact has been long considered 'superfluous', and because of the rushed way in which it was conceived, NATO officials labeled it as a 'cardboard castle'. Previously, in March 1954, the USSR, fearing the restoration of German Militarism in West Germany, requested admission to NATO.
rewrite: Fearing a rearmed Germany, Czechoslovak leadership initially sought a security pact with East Germany and Poland before the Warsaw Pact's creation, as these states strongly protested West Germany's re-militarization. The Pact was primarily established in response to West Germany joining NATO. Soviet leaders, alongside many European nations on both sides, viewed the prospect of Germany again becoming a military power as a direct threat, with German militarism remaining a fresh memory. Although the Soviet Union already had bilateral treaties with its eastern satellites, making the Pact seem 'superfluous', its hastily conceived nature led NATO officials to dismiss it as a 'cardboard castle'. Earlier, in March 1954, the USSR had even sought NATO admission, driven by these same fears of resurgent German militarism.

input: Racial discrimination continued to be enacted in new laws in the 20th century, for instance the one-drop rule was enacted in Virginia's 1924 Racial Integrity Law and in other southern states, in part influenced by the popularity of eugenics and ideas of racial purity. People buried fading memories that many whites had multiracial ancestry. Many families were multiracial. Similar laws had been proposed but not passed in the late nineteenth century in South Carolina and Virginia, for instance. After regaining political power in Southern states by disenfranchising blacks, white Democrats passed laws to impose Jim Crow and racial segregation to restore white supremacy. They maintained these until forced to change in the 1960s and after by enforcement of federal legislation authorizing oversight of practices to protect the constitutional rights of African Americans and other minority citizens.
rewrite: In the 20th century, new laws continued to enact racial discrimination. Influenced by eugenics and notions of racial purity, states like Virginia passed measures such as the 1924 Racial Integrity Law, which included the one-drop rule, and other southern states followed. This occurred despite fading memories of the multiracial ancestry common among many white families and the fact that many households were themselves multiracial. Earlier versions of such laws had been proposed, though not passed, in the late nineteenth century in states like South Carolina and Virginia. Having regained political power through the disenfranchisement of Black voters, white Democrats imposed Jim Crow segregation to restore white supremacy. They maintained this system until the 1960s and beyond, when federal legislation was enforced to protect the constitutional rights of African Americans and other minorities.

input: Breeding usually involves some form of courtship display, typically performed by the male. Most displays are rather simple and involve some type of song. Some displays, however, are quite elaborate. Depending on the species, these may include wing or tail drumming, dancing, aerial flights, or communal lekking. Females are generally the ones that drive partner selection, although in the polyandrous phalaropes, this is reversed: plainer males choose brightly coloured females. Courtship feeding, billing and allopreening are commonly performed between partners, generally after the birds have paired and mated.
rewrite: Courtship displays, often performed by males, typically involve simple songs, though some species exhibit more elaborate behaviors. These can include wing or tail drumming, dancing, aerial flights, or communal lekking. While females usually select their partners, this is reversed in polyandrous phalaropes, where plainer males choose brightly colored females. After pairing and mating, partners commonly engage in courtship feeding, billing, and allopreening.

input: The Staten Island Ferry is the world's busiest ferry route, carrying approximately 20 million passengers on the 5.2-mile (8.4 km) route between Staten Island and Lower Manhattan and running 24 hours a day. Other ferry systems shuttle commuters between Manhattan and other locales within the city and the metropolitan area.
rewrite: Operating 24 hours daily, the Staten Island Ferry transports about 20 million passengers along its 5.2-mile route, making it the world's busiest. Additional ferry systems also connect Manhattan to other parts of the city and wider metropolitan area for commuters.

input: The concept's origins can potentially be traced back further. Jewish law includes several considerations whose effects are similar to those of modern intellectual property laws, though the notion of intellectual creations as property does not seem to exist – notably the principle of Hasagat Ge'vul (unfair encroachment) was used to justify limited-term publisher (but not author) copyright in the 16th century. In 500 BCE, the government of the Greek state of Sybaris offered one year's patent "to all who should discover any new refinement in luxury".
rewrite: While the modern idea of intellectual creations as property was absent, precursors to intellectual property concepts emerged much earlier. In the 16th century, Jewish law's principle of Hasagat Ge'vul (unfair encroachment) supported limited copyright for publishers. Even earlier, around 500 BCE, the Greek state of Sybaris granted a one-year patent to inventors of new luxuries. Thus, the origins of these legal ideas can be traced back to ancient and early modern practices.

input: In addition, the Prussian military education system was superior to the French model; Prussian staff officers were trained to exhibit initiative and independent thinking. Indeed, this was Moltke's expectation. The French, meanwhile, suffered from an education and promotion system that stifled intellectual development. According to the military historian Dallas Irvine, the system "was almost completely effective in excluding the army's brain power from the staff and high command. To the resulting lack of intelligence at the top can be ascribed all the inexcusable defects of French military policy."
rewrite: The Prussian military education system surpassed the French model by training staff officers to demonstrate initiative and independent thought, precisely as Moltke intended. Conversely, the French system of education and promotion suppressed intellectual growth. Military historian Dallas Irvine states it "was almost completely effective in excluding the army's brain power from the staff and high command," a deficiency he blames for all the inexcusable flaws in French military policy.

input: Stemmatics, stemmology or stemmatology is a rigorous approach to textual criticism. Karl Lachmann (1793–1851) greatly contributed to making this method famous, even though he did not invent it. The method takes its name from the word stemma. The Ancient Greek word στέμματα and its loanword in classical Latin stemmata may refer to "family trees". This specific meaning shows the relationships of the surviving witnesses (the first known example of such a stemma, albeit with the name, dates from 1827). The family tree is also referred to as a cladogram. The method works from the principle that "community of error implies community of origin." That is, if two witnesses have a number of errors in common, it may be presumed that they were derived from a common intermediate source, called a hyparchetype. Relations between the lost intermediates are determined by the same process, placing all extant manuscripts in a family tree or stemma codicum descended from a single archetype. The process of constructing the stemma is called recension, or the Latin recensio.
rewrite: Stemmatics, also known as stemmology or stemmatology, represents a rigorous method within textual criticism. The term derives from "stemma," with the Ancient Greek στέμματα and its Latin counterpart stemmata carrying the meaning of "family trees." This specific sense illustrates the relationships among surviving manuscript witnesses. The approach operates on the principle that "community of error implies community of origin." Consequently, when two witnesses share a set of errors, they are presumed to descend from a common intermediate source, termed a hyparchetype. By repeating this process for lost intermediates, all extant manuscripts are placed within a family tree, or stemma codicum, ultimately descended from a single archetype. Although Karl Lachmann (1793–1851) did not invent the method, he played a major role in popularizing it. The first known named example of such a stemma dates from 1827. This family tree structure is also called a cladogram, and the process of constructing it is known as recension, from the Latin recensio.

input: Although a resonant antenna has a purely resistive feed-point impedance at a particular frequency, many (if not most) applications require using an antenna over a range of frequencies. An antenna's bandwidth specifies the range of frequencies over which its performance does not suffer due to a poor impedance match. Also in the case of a Yagi-Uda array, the use of the antenna very far away from its design frequency reduces the antenna's directivity, thus reducing the usable bandwidth regardless of impedance matching.
rewrite: While many applications require an antenna to function across a range of frequencies, a resonant antenna only has a purely resistive impedance at one specific frequency. The antenna's bandwidth defines the frequencies where performance remains acceptable despite impedance mismatch. Furthermore, for antennas like a Yagi-Uda array, operating too far from the design frequency reduces directivity. This decrease in directivity limits the usable bandwidth independently of any impedance matching issues.

input: Peer groups are essential to social and general development. Communication with peers increases significantly during adolescence and peer relationships become more intense than in other stages  and more influential to the teen, affecting both the decisions and choices being made. High quality friendships may enhance children's development regardless of the characteristics of those friends. As children begin to bond with various people and create friendships, it later helps them when they are adolescent and sets up the framework for adolescence and peer groups. Peer groups are especially important during adolescence, a period of development characterized by a dramatic increase in time spent with peers and a decrease in adult supervision. Adolescents also associate with friends of the opposite sex much more than in childhood and tend to identify with larger groups of peers based on shared characteristics. It is also common for adolescents to use friends as coping devices in different situations. A three-factor structure of dealing with friends including avoidance, mastery, and nonchalance has shown that adolescents use friends as coping devices with social stresses.
rewrite:
During adolescence, peer groups become especially vital for social and general development. This period is marked by a dramatic increase in time spent with peers and a corresponding decrease in adult supervision. Communication with peers intensifies significantly, and these relationships grow more influential, directly shaping the decisions and choices teens make. As children form early bonds and friendships, they establish a crucial framework that supports them in adolescence. Notably, high-quality friendships can enhance development independently of the friends' specific characteristics.

Adolescents also expand their social circles, associating with friends of the opposite sex far more than in childhood and often identifying with larger peer groups based on shared traits. Furthermore, friends are frequently used as coping devices to navigate various situations. Research into how adolescents manage social stress has identified a three-factor structure—avoidance, mastery, and nonchalance—demonstrating the specific ways friends serve as resources for coping.

input: Israel operates under a parliamentary system as a democratic republic with universal suffrage. A member of parliament supported by a parliamentary majority becomes the prime minister—usually this is the chair of the largest party. The prime minister is the head of government and head of the cabinet. Israel is governed by a 120-member parliament, known as the Knesset. Membership of the Knesset is based on proportional representation of political parties, with a 3.25% electoral threshold, which in practice has resulted in coalition governments.
rewrite: Israel functions as a democratic republic with universal suffrage, governed by a 120-member parliament called the Knesset. The prime minister, who serves as head of government and cabinet, is typically the chair of the largest party and must command a parliamentary majority. Knesset seats are allocated through proportional representation among political parties that meet a 3.25% electoral threshold. This system has consistently led to the formation of coalition governments.

input: However, from 1971 to 1975, NBA teams played preseason exhibitions against American Basketball Association teams. In the early days of the NBA, league clubs sometimes challenged the legendary barnstorming Harlem Globetrotters, with mixed success. The NBA has played preseason games in Europe and Asia. In the 2006 and 2007 seasons, the NBA and the primary European club competition, the Euroleague, conducted a preseason tournament featuring two NBA teams and the finalists from that year's Euroleague.[citation needed] In the 1998-99 and 2011-12 seasons, teams were limited to only two preseason games due to lockouts.
rewrite: From 1971 to 1975, NBA teams faced American Basketball Association clubs in preseason exhibitions. Preseason games have also been held internationally in Europe and Asia. In the NBA's early years, teams occasionally competed against the famed barnstorming Harlem Globetrotters, achieving varied results. A special preseason tournament occurred in 2006 and 2007, involving two NBA teams and the Euroleague finalists. Notably, during the lockout-shortened seasons of 1998-99 and 2011-12, teams were restricted to just two preseason contests.

input: Traditionally, the Speaker is reckoned as the leader of the majority party in the House, with the Majority Leader as second-in-command. For instance, when the Republicans gained the majority in the House after the 2010 elections, Eric Cantor succeeded Boehner as Majority Leader. Despite this, Cantor and his successor, Kevin McCarthy, have been reckoned as the second-ranking Republicans in the House, since Boehner is still reckoned as the leader of the House Republicans. However, there have been some exceptions. The most recent exception to this rule came when Majority Leader Tom DeLay generally overshadowed Speaker Dennis Hastert from 2003 to 2006. In contrast, the Minority Leader is the undisputed leader of the minority party.
rewrite: In the House, the Speaker is traditionally considered the leader of the majority party, followed by the Majority Leader as second-in-command. For example, Eric Cantor became Majority Leader after the Republican majority was secured in the 2010 elections. Both he and his successor, Kevin McCarthy, have been viewed as the second-ranking House Republicans, with John Boehner still seen as the party leader. Exceptions to this structure do occur, most notably from 2003 to 2006 when Majority Leader Tom DeLay largely overshadowed Speaker Dennis Hastert. Conversely, the Minority Leader holds undisputed authority within the minority party.

input: Molotov declared in his report entitled "On the Foreign Policy of the Soviet Union" (31 October 1939) held on the fifth (extraordinary) session of the Supreme Soviet, that the Western "ruling circles" disguise their intentions with the pretext of defending democracy against Hitlerism, declaring "their aim in war with Germany is nothing more, nothing less than extermination of Hitlerism. [...] There is absolutely no justification for this kind of war. The ideology of Hitlerism, just like any other ideological system, can be accepted or rejected, this is a matter of political views. But everyone grasps, that an ideology can not be exterminated by force, must not be finished off with a war."
rewrite: In his report "On the Foreign Policy of the Soviet Union," delivered at the fifth extraordinary session of the Supreme Soviet on 31 October 1939, Molotov addressed the Western "ruling circles." He asserted that they masked their true intentions by claiming to defend democracy against Hitlerism, stating their war aim was "nothing more, nothing less than extermination of Hitlerism." Molotov condemned this, arguing, "There is absolutely no justification for this kind of war." He maintained that Hitlerism, as an ideology, could be accepted or rejected as a political matter. However, he insisted everyone understands that "an ideology can not be exterminated by force, must not be finished off with a war."

input: Instruments were marketed by teacher-dealers, much as the title character in the popular musical The Music Man. Often, these teacher-dealers conducted mandolin orchestras: groups of 4-50 musicians who played various mandolin family instruments. However, alongside the teacher-dealers were serious musicians, working to create a spot for the instrument in classical music, ragtime and jazz. Like the teacher-dealers, they traveled the U.S., recording records, giving performances and teaching individuals and mandolin orchestras. Samuel Siegel played mandolin in Vaudeville and became one of America's preeminent mandolinists. Seth Weeks was an African American who not only taught and performed in the United States, but also in Europe, where he recorded records. Another pioneering African American musician and director who made his start with a mandolin orchestra was composer James Reese Europe. W. Eugene Page toured the country with a group, and was well known for his mandolin and mandola performances. Other names include Valentine Abt, Samuel Adelstein, William Place, Jr., and Aubrey Stauffer.
rewrite: Much like the charismatic salesman in *The Music Man*, instruments were often promoted by teacher-dealers. These individuals frequently led mandolin orchestras, ensembles ranging from four to fifty musicians playing various instruments from the mandolin family. Yet the scene also included serious musicians dedicated to establishing the mandolin within classical, ragtime, and jazz. They, too, traveled across the United States, recording, performing, and teaching both individuals and orchestras. Among the notable figures was Samuel Siegel, a Vaudeville performer who rose to become a preeminent American mandolinist. Seth Weeks, an African American musician, taught and performed not only in the U.S. but also in Europe, where he made recordings. Another pioneering African American composer and director, James Reese Europe, began his career with a mandolin orchestra. W. Eugene Page toured nationally with his group, gaining renown for his skill on the mandolin and mandola. Further contributors included Valentine Abt, Samuel Adelstein, William Place, Jr., and Aubrey Stauffer.

input: Ethnically and linguistically the population of the Republic of the Congo is diverse—Ethnologue recognises 62 spoken languages in the country—but can be grouped into three categories. The Kongo are the largest ethnic group and form roughly half of the population. The most significant subgroups of the Kongo are Laari in Brazzaville and Pool regions and Vili around Pointe-Noire and along the Atlantic coast. The second largest group are the Teke who live to the north of Brazzaville with 17% of the population. Boulangui (M’Boshi) live in the northwest and in Brazzaville and form 12% of the population. Pygmies make up 2% of Congo's population.
rewrite: The Republic of the Congo's population is ethnically and linguistically diverse, with 62 spoken languages recognized by Ethnologue. This diversity can be broadly categorized into three main groups. The Kongo people are the largest, constituting about half of the population, with key subgroups including the Laari in Brazzaville and Pool and the Vili around Pointe-Noire. The Teke, forming 17%, are the second-largest group and reside north of Brazzaville. Meanwhile, the Boulangui (M’Boshi) account for 12%, living in the northwest and Brazzaville, and Pygmies represent 2% of the inhabitants.

input: At the end of the 12th century, Europe was divided into a multitude of city states and kingdoms. The area encompassing modern Germany, southern Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Austria, Slovakia, Czech Republic and much of northern Italy (excluding Venice and Papal State) was nominally part of the Holy Roman Empire, but local rulers exercised considerable autonomy. France, Denmark, Poland, Hungary, Portugal, Scotland, Castile, Aragon, Navarre, Sicily and Cyprus were independent kingdoms, as was the Angevin Empire, whose Plantagenet kings ruled England and large domains in what was to become modern France. Norway came under the influence of England, while the other Scandinavian countries and Poland were influenced by trading contacts with the Hanseatic League. Angevin kings brought the Gothic tradition from France to Southern Italy, while Lusignan kings introduced French Gothic architecture to Cyprus.
rewrite: By the close of the 12th century, Europe consisted of numerous independent kingdoms and city states. Among these were France, Denmark, Poland, Hungary, Portugal, Scotland, Castile, Aragon, Navarre, Sicily, and Cyprus. The Plantagenet-ruled Angevin Empire, holding England and extensive French territories, was another sovereign realm. Nominally, the Holy Roman Empire covered a vast region including modern Germany, southern Denmark, the Low Countries, Switzerland, Austria, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, and much of northern Italy, though local rulers held significant power. Norway fell under English influence, while other Scandinavian lands and Poland were affected by Hanseatic League trade. Architecturally, Angevin rulers carried the Gothic style from France to Southern Italy, and the Lusignan kings brought French Gothic forms to Cyprus.

input: On December 3, 2013, Adidas officially confirmed a new shoe collaboration deal with West. After months of anticipation and rumors, West confirmed the release of the Adidas Yeezy Boosts with a Twitter announcement directing fans to the domain yeezy.supply. In 2015, West unveiled his Yeezy Season clothing line, premiering Season 1 in collaboration with Adidas early in the year. The release of the Yeezy Boosts and the full Adidas collaboration was showcased in New York City on February 12, 2015, with free streaming to 50 cinemas in 13 countries around the world. An initial release of the Adidas Yeezy Boosts was limited to 9000 pairs to be available only in New York City via the Adidas smartphone app; the Adidas Yeezy Boosts were sold out within 10 minutes. The shoes released worldwide on February 28, 2015, were limited to select boutique stores and the Adidas UK stores. He followed with Season 2 later that year at New York Fashion Week. On February 11, West premiered his Yeezy Season 3 clothing line at Madison Square Garden in conjunction with the previewing of his album The Life of Pablo.
rewrite: Adidas formally announced a new collaborative shoe agreement with West on December 3, 2013. Following months of speculation, West himself confirmed the upcoming Adidas Yeezy Boosts via Twitter, guiding followers to the website yeezy.supply. The full collaboration, including these shoes, was first presented in New York City on February 12, 2015, with a simultaneous free stream to 50 cinemas across 13 nations. An extremely limited initial release of just 9000 pairs was made available exclusively in New York City through the Adidas app, selling out in under ten minutes. A global release followed on February 28, 2015, restricted to chosen boutique shops and Adidas UK stores. Earlier in 2015, West had introduced his Yeezy Season 1 apparel line with Adidas. He continued with Season 2 later that year during New York Fashion Week. Subsequently, on February 11 the following year, West debuted his Yeezy Season 3 collection at Madison Square Garden, paired with a preview of his album *The Life of Pablo*.

input: Synapses are the key functional elements of the brain. The essential function of the brain is cell-to-cell communication, and synapses are the points at which communication occurs. The human brain has been estimated to contain approximately 100 trillion synapses; even the brain of a fruit fly contains several million. The functions of these synapses are very diverse: some are excitatory (exciting the target cell); others are inhibitory; others work by activating second messenger systems that change the internal chemistry of their target cells in complex ways. A large number of synapses are dynamically modifiable; that is, they are capable of changing strength in a way that is controlled by the patterns of signals that pass through them. It is widely believed that activity-dependent modification of synapses is the brain's primary mechanism for learning and memory.
rewrite: The brain's essential function of cell-to-cell communication occurs at specialized points called synapses, making them its key functional elements. While a fruit fly brain holds several million, the human brain contains an estimated 100 trillion of these junctions. Their roles are highly diverse: some excite target cells, others inhibit, and some activate complex internal chemical changes via second messenger systems. Crucially, a vast number of synapses are dynamically modifiable, meaning their strength can change based on the patterns of signals they transmit. This activity-dependent modification is widely considered the primary mechanism for learning and memory in the brain.

input: The highest portion of the range is divided by the glacial trough of the Rhone valley, with the Pennine Alps from Mont Blanc to the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa on the southern side, and the Bernese Alps on the northern. The peaks in the easterly portion of the range, in Austria and Slovenia, are smaller than those in the central and western portions.
rewrite: The Rhone valley's glacial trough splits the range's highest part, flanked by the Pennine Alps to the south and the Bernese Alps to the north. While the central and western areas contain larger peaks, those in the eastern portion within Austria and Slovenia are comparatively smaller.

input: There are two basic forms of data packet, DATA0 and DATA1. A data packet must always be preceded by an address token, and is usually followed by a handshake token from the receiver back to the transmitter. The two packet types provide the 1-bit sequence number required by Stop-and-wait ARQ. If a USB host does not receive a response (such as an ACK) for data it has transmitted, it does not know if the data was received or not; the data might have been lost in transit, or it might have been received but the handshake response was lost.
rewrite: Data packets come in two basic types: DATA0 and DATA1. Each must be preceded by an address token and is typically followed by a handshake token from the receiver back to the transmitter. These two packet types supply the 1-bit sequence number needed for Stop-and-wait ARQ. If a USB host transmits data but gets no response like an ACK, it cannot determine whether the data was received. The data may have been lost during transmission, or it might have arrived while the handshake was lost.

input: Charleston has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification Cfa), with mild winters, hot, humid summers, and significant rainfall all year long. Summer is the wettest season; almost half of the annual rainfall occurs from June to September in the form of thundershowers. Fall remains relatively warm through November. Winter is short and mild, and is characterized by occasional rain. Measurable snow (≥0.1 in or 0.25 cm) only occurs several times per decade at the most, with the last such event occurring December 26, 2010. However, 6.0 in (15 cm) fell at the airport on December 23, 1989, the largest single-day fall on record, contributing to a single-storm and seasonal record of 8.0 in (20 cm) snowfall.
rewrite: Charleston experiences a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa), featuring mild winters and hot, humid summers with year-round precipitation. The wettest period is summer, when nearly half the annual rain falls as thundershowers from June through September. Winters are short and mild, often marked by occasional rain. Snowfall is rare, with measurable amounts only occurring a few times per decade; the last recorded instance was on December 26, 2010. The most significant snowfall on record happened on December 23, 1989, when 6.0 inches (15 cm) fell at the airport in a single day. This event contributed to a record seasonal and single-storm total of 8.0 inches (20 cm). Fall stays relatively warm into November.

input: Murdoch found he had such a rapport with Larry Lamb over lunch that other potential recruits as editor were not interviewed and Lamb was appointed as the first editor of the new Sun. He was scathing in his opinion of the Mirror, where he had recently been employed as a senior sub-editor, and shared Murdoch's view that a paper's quality was best measured by its sales, and he regarded the Mirror as overstaffed, and primarily aimed at an ageing readership. Lamb hastily recruited a staff of about 125 reporters, who were mostly selected for their availability rather than their ability.
rewrite: Murdoch felt an immediate connection with Larry Lamb during their lunch, leading him to skip other interviews and directly appoint Lamb as the inaugural editor of the Sun. Lamb, who had recently worked as a senior sub-editor at the Mirror, was highly critical of his former employer. He agreed with Murdoch that sales were the true measure of a newspaper's success, viewing the Mirror as bloated with staff and catering mainly to an older audience. Quickly assembling a team, Lamb hired approximately 125 reporters, prioritizing their immediate availability over their journalistic skill.

input: The four-year, full-time undergraduate program comprises the majority of enrollments at the university and emphasizes instruction in the arts and sciences, plus the professions of engineering, journalism, communication, music, and education. Although a foundation in the liberal arts and sciences is required in all majors, there is no required common core curriculum; individual degree requirements are set by the faculty of each school. Northwestern's full-time undergraduate and graduate programs operate on an approximately 10-week academic quarter system with the academic year beginning in late September and ending in early June. Undergraduates typically take four courses each quarter and twelve courses in an academic year and are required to complete at least twelve quarters on campus to graduate. Northwestern offers honors, accelerated, and joint degree programs in medicine, science, mathematics, engineering, and journalism. The comprehensive doctoral graduate program has high coexistence with undergraduate programs.
rewrite: At Northwestern University, the primary academic structure is a four-year, full-time undergraduate program, which focuses on arts, sciences, and professional fields like engineering, journalism, communication, music, and education. While all majors include a foundation in liberal arts and sciences, there is no common core curriculum; instead, each school’s faculty determines specific degree requirements. The university operates on a 10-week quarter system, running from late September to early June. Full-time undergraduates generally enroll in four courses per quarter, totaling twelve annually, and must complete at least twelve quarters on campus to graduate. Honors, accelerated, and joint degree options are available in areas such as medicine, science, mathematics, engineering, and journalism. Additionally, the comprehensive doctoral program closely coexists with undergraduate offerings.

input: In 2010, a genetic study was conducted on the mummified remains of baboons that were brought back as gifts from Punt by the ancient Egyptians. Led by a research team from the Egyptian Museum and the University of California, the scientists used oxygen isotope analysis to examine hairs from two baboon mummies that had been preserved in the British Museum. One of the baboons had distorted isotopic data, so the other's oxygen isotope values were compared to those of present-day baboon specimens from regions of interest. The researchers found that the mummies most closely matched modern baboon specimens in Eritrea and Ethiopia, which they suggested implied that Punt was likely a narrow region that included eastern Ethiopia and all of Eritrea.
rewrite: A 2010 genetic study analyzed mummified baboons, gifts brought from Punt by ancient Egyptians. Scientists from the Egyptian Museum and the University of California performed oxygen isotope analysis on hairs from two baboon mummies housed in the British Museum. After one specimen's data proved distorted, they compared the other's oxygen isotope values to those of modern baboons from various regions. The closest match was to present-day specimens from Eritrea and eastern Ethiopia. This led the research team to conclude that Punt was likely a confined area encompassing eastern Ethiopia and all of Eritrea.

input: After the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, Emperor Nero accused the Christians as convenient scapegoats, who were later persecuted and killed. From that point on, Roman official policy towards Christianity tended towards persecution. During the various Imperial crises of the 3rd century, “contemporaries were predisposed to decode any crisis in religious terms”, regardless of their allegiance to particular practices or belief systems. Christianity drew its traditional base of support from the powerless, who seemed to have no religious stake in the well-being of the Roman State, and therefore threatened its existence. The majority of Rome’s elite continued to observe various forms of inclusive Hellenistic monism; Neoplatonism in particular accommodated the miraculous and the ascetic within a traditional Graeco-Roman cultic framework. Christians saw these ungodly practices as a primary cause of economic and political crisis.
rewrite: In the wake of Rome’s Great Fire of 64 AD, Emperor Nero targeted Christians as scapegoats, leading to their persecution and execution. This established a pattern of official Roman hostility toward the faith. The powerless, who formed Christianity’s core support, were seen as having no stake in the state’s stability and thus posed a threat. During the third century’s imperial crises, people widely interpreted disasters through a religious lens. Meanwhile, most of Rome’s elite adhered to inclusive Hellenistic monism, especially Neoplatonism, which integrated the miraculous into traditional Graeco-Roman worship. Christians, however, viewed these practices as ungodly and a fundamental cause of the empire’s economic and political turmoil.

input: The first non-stop transatlantic crossing was made by the British airship R34 in 1919. Regular passenger service resumed in the 1920s and the discovery of helium reserves in the United States promised increased safety, but the U.S. government refused to sell the gas for this purpose. Therefore, H2 was used in the Hindenburg airship, which was destroyed in a midair fire over New Jersey on 6 May 1937. The incident was broadcast live on radio and filmed. Ignition of leaking hydrogen is widely assumed to be the cause, but later investigations pointed to the ignition of the aluminized fabric coating by static electricity. But the damage to hydrogen's reputation as a lifting gas was already done.
rewrite: In 1919, the British airship R34 completed the first non-stop transatlantic crossing. Though regular passenger flights resumed in the 1920s and U.S. helium reserves offered a safer alternative, the government prohibited its sale for this use. Consequently, the Hindenburg airship was filled with hydrogen. It was destroyed in a fiery crash over New Jersey on May 6, 1937, an event broadcast live on radio and captured on film. While the ignition of leaking hydrogen is the commonly cited cause, later investigations suggested static electricity ignited the aluminized fabric coating. Regardless, the disaster permanently tarnished hydrogen's reputation as a lifting gas.

input: A 2009 Cochrane review concluded that thiazide antihypertensive drugs reduce the risk of death (RR 0.89), stroke (RR 0.63), coronary heart disease (RR 0.84), and cardiovascular events (RR 0.70) in people with high blood pressure. In the ensuring years other classes of antihypertensive drug were developed and found wide acceptance in combination therapy, including loop diuretics (Lasix/furosemide, Hoechst Pharmaceuticals, 1963), beta blockers (ICI Pharmaceuticals, 1964) ACE inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor blockers. ACE inhibitors reduce the risk of new onset kidney disease [RR 0.71] and death [RR 0.84] in diabetic patients, irrespective of whether they have hypertension.
rewrite: Thiazide antihypertensive drugs were found in a 2009 Cochrane review to lower risks of death (RR 0.89), stroke (RR 0.63), coronary heart disease (RR 0.84), and cardiovascular events (RR 0.70) in hypertensive patients. Subsequent years saw the development and widespread use of other drug classes in combination therapy, such as loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide, 1963), beta blockers (1964), ACE inhibitors, and angiotensin receptor blockers. For diabetic patients, ACE inhibitors reduce the risk of new kidney disease (RR 0.71) and death (RR 0.84), even without hypertension.

input: A count may be started at any time that a wrestler's shoulders are down (both shoulders touching the mat), back-first and any part of the opponent's body is lying over the wrestler. This often results in pins that can easily be kicked out of, if the defensive wrestler is even slightly conscious. For example, an attacking wrestler who is half-conscious may simply drape an arm over an opponent, or a cocky wrestler may place their foot gently on the opponent's body, prompting a three-count from the referee.
rewrite: A pin can be initiated whenever a wrestler is on their back with both shoulders touching the mat and any part of the opponent is lying over them. This frequently leads to precarious pins that a defensive wrestler can escape with minimal awareness. For instance, a barely conscious attacker might merely lay an arm across an opponent, or an arrogant wrestler could lightly rest a foot on their foe, each action triggering the referee's three-count.

input: The Republic of Letters was the sum of a number of Enlightenment ideals: an egalitarian realm governed by knowledge that could act across political boundaries and rival state power. It was a forum that supported "free public examination of questions regarding religion or legislation". Immanuel Kant considered written communication essential to his conception of the public sphere; once everyone was a part of the "reading public", then society could be said to be enlightened. The people who participated in the Republic of Letters, such as Diderot and Voltaire, are frequently known today as important Enlightenment figures. Indeed, the men who wrote Diderot's Encyclopédie arguably formed a microcosm of the larger "republic".
rewrite: Encompassing key Enlightenment ideals, the Republic of Letters was an egalitarian domain governed by knowledge, transcending political borders and challenging state authority. It served as a forum committed to the free public scrutiny of religion and legislation. Participants like Diderot and Voltaire, now celebrated as major Enlightenment thinkers, engaged in this realm. Immanuel Kant viewed written communication as fundamental to the public sphere, believing an enlightened society required a universal "reading public." Notably, the contributors to Diderot's Encyclopédie themselves represented a microcosm of this broader republic.

input: The Chicago Cubs have not won a World Series championship since 1908, and have not appeared in the Fall Classic since 1945, although between their postseason appearance in 1984 and their most recent in 2015, they have made the postseason seven times. 107 seasons is the longest championship drought in all four of the major North American professional sports leagues, which also includes the National Football League (NFL), the National Basketball Association (NBA), and the National Hockey League (NHL). In fact, the Cubs' last World Series title occurred before those other three leagues even existed, and even the Cubs' last World Series appearance predates the founding of the NBA. The much publicized drought was concurrent to championship droughts by the Boston Red Sox and the Chicago White Sox, who both had over 80 years between championships. It is this unfortunate distinction that has led to the club often being known as "The Lovable Losers." The team was one win away from breaking what is often called the "Curse of the Billy Goat" in 1984 and 2003 (Steve Bartman incident), but was unable get the victory that would send it to the World Series.
rewrite: Despite making seven postseason appearances between 1984 and 2015, the Chicago Cubs have not won a World Series since 1908, nor have they played in one since 1945. This stretch of 107 seasons represents the longest championship drought across all four major North American professional sports leagues—the NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLB.
