The Cubs’ last title predates the existence of the other three leagues, and their last World Series appearance even occurred before the NBA was founded. For much of this period, their plight was shared by the Boston Red Sox and Chicago White Sox, who each endured over 80 years between championships. This lengthy misfortune earned the Cubs the nickname “The Lovable Losers.” The team came within a single victory of ending the so-called “Curse of the Billy Goat” in both 1984 and 2003—the latter infamously involving the Steve Bartman incident—but fell short of reaching the World Series each time.

input: The Carnival of Malmedy is locally called Cwarmê. Even if Malmedy is located in the east Belgium, near the German-speaking area, the Cwarmê is a pure walloon and Latin carnival. The celebration takes place during 4 days before the Shrove Tuesday. The Cwarmê Sunday is the most important and insteresting to see. All the old traditional costumes parade in the street. The Cwarmê is a "street carnival" and is not only a parade. People who are disguised pass through the crowd and perform a part of the traditional costume they wear. The famous traditional costumes at the Cwarmê of Malmedy are the Haguète, the Longuès-Brèsses and the Long-Né.
rewrite: Known locally as Cwarmê, the Carnival of Malmedy is a distinctly Walloon and Latin celebration, despite the town's location in eastern Belgium near German-speaking regions. Held over the four days preceding Shrove Tuesday, it is a vibrant "street carnival," not merely a parade. The highlight is Cwarmê Sunday, when traditional costumes fill the streets. Disguised participants move through the crowds, actively performing elements of their roles. Key figures include the Haguète, the Longuès-Brèsses, and the Long-Né.

input: On February 7, 1987, dozens of political prisoners were freed in the first group release since Khrushchev's "thaw" in the mid-1950s. On May 6, 1987, Pamyat, a Russian nationalist group, held an unsanctioned demonstration in Moscow. The authorities did not break up the demonstration and even kept traffic out of the demonstrators' way while they marched to an impromptu meeting with Boris Yeltsin, head of the Moscow Communist Party and at the time one of Gorbachev's closest allies. On July 25, 1987, 300 Crimean Tatars staged a noisy demonstration near the Kremlin Wall for several hours, calling for the right to return to their homeland, from which they were deported in 1944; police and soldiers merely looked on.
rewrite: In a notable shift, dozens of political prisoners were freed on February 7, 1987, marking the first such group release since Khrushchev's mid-1950s "thaw." That May 6, the Russian nationalist group Pamyat staged an unsanctioned Moscow demonstration. Authorities not only refrained from breaking it up but also diverted traffic as marchers proceeded to an impromptu meeting with Boris Yeltsin, then Moscow's Communist Party head and a key Gorbachev ally. Later, on July 25, 300 Crimean Tatars held a hours-long, noisy protest near the Kremlin Wall, demanding the right to return to their homeland, from which they were deported in 1944; police and soldiers merely observed.

input: The length and nature of parental care varies widely amongst different orders and species. At one extreme, parental care in megapodes ends at hatching; the newly hatched chick digs itself out of the nest mound without parental assistance and can fend for itself immediately. At the other extreme, many seabirds have extended periods of parental care, the longest being that of the great frigatebird, whose chicks take up to six months to fledge and are fed by the parents for up to an additional 14 months. The chick guard stage describes the period of breeding during which one of the adult birds is permanently present at the nest after chicks have hatched. The main purpose of the guard stage is to aid offspring to thermoregulate and protect them from predation.
rewrite: Parental care differs greatly in duration and form across bird orders and species. In some cases, like the megapodes, it concludes at hatching; chicks independently dig out from the nest mound and are instantly self-sufficient. Conversely, many seabirds exhibit prolonged care, with the great frigatebird representing an extreme: chicks require up to six months to fledge and then receive parental feeding for as long as 14 more months. Following hatching, a chick guard stage occurs, where an adult remains constantly at the nest. This phase primarily assists offspring in regulating body temperature and shields them from predators.

input: In Virginia prior to 1920, for example, a person was legally white if having seven-eights or more white ancestry. The one-drop rule originated in some Southern United States in the late 19th century, likely in response to whites' attempt to maintain white supremacy and limit black political power following the Democrats' regaining control of state legislatures in the late 1870s. The first year in which the U.S. Census dropped the mulatto category was 1920; that year enumerators were instructed to classify people in a binary way as white or black. This was a result of the Southern-dominated Congress convincing the Census Bureau to change its rules.
rewrite: In the late 19th century, the one-drop rule emerged in some Southern U.S. states, largely as a white supremacist effort to restrict Black political power after Democrats retook control of state legislatures in the 1870s. Earlier, places like Virginia had defined legal whiteness as having at least seven-eighths white ancestry. A significant shift occurred in 1920, when the U.S. Census eliminated the "mulatto" category. Under pressure from a Southern-dominated Congress, the Census Bureau instructed enumerators to classify people only as either white or black, cementing a strict racial binary.

input: A sequence of events, or series of events, is a sequence of items, facts, events, actions, changes, or procedural steps, arranged in time order (chronological order), often with causality relationships among the items. Because of causality, cause precedes effect, or cause and effect may appear together in a single item, but effect never precedes cause. A sequence of events can be presented in text, tables, charts, or timelines. The description of the items or events may include a timestamp. A sequence of events that includes the time along with place or location information to describe a sequential path may be referred to as a world line.
rewrite: A sequence of events arranges items—such as facts, actions, or changes—in chronological order, often showing causal links. In these relationships, a cause always comes before or coincides with its effect, never after. This sequence can be depicted through text, tables, charts, or timelines, sometimes incorporating timestamps. When the description also tracks location over time, forming a sequential path, it may be termed a world line. Essentially, it is a structured series where time order and causality connect the elements.

input: According to the prevailing theories of the settlement of the Americas, migrations of humans from Asia (in particular North Asia) to the Americas took place via Beringia, a land bridge which connected the two continents across what is now the Bering Strait. The majority of experts agree that the earliest pre-modern human migration via Beringia took place at least 13,500 years ago, with disputed evidence that people had migrated into the Americas much earlier, up to 40,000 years ago. These early Paleo-Indians spread throughout the Americas, diversifying into many hundreds of culturally distinct nations and tribes. According to the oral histories of many of the indigenous peoples of the Americas, they have been living there since their genesis, described by a wide range of creation myths.
rewrite: The Americas were settled by humans migrating from Asia, primarily North Asia, across a land bridge known as Beringia, now the Bering Strait. While most experts concur that the earliest confirmed migration occurred at least 13,500 years ago, some disputed evidence suggests movements as early as 40,000 years ago. These first peoples, the Paleo-Indians, subsequently spread and diversified into hundreds of distinct cultures and tribes. In contrast, the oral traditions and creation myths of many indigenous peoples describe their presence in the Americas since their very origins.

input: The denomination with the longest history of objection to Freemasonry is the Roman Catholic Church. The objections raised by the Roman Catholic Church are based on the allegation that Masonry teaches a naturalistic deistic religion which is in conflict with Church doctrine. A number of Papal pronouncements have been issued against Freemasonry. The first was Pope Clement XII's In eminenti apostolatus, 28 April 1738; the most recent was Pope Leo XIII's Ab apostolici, 15 October 1890. The 1917 Code of Canon Law explicitly declared that joining Freemasonry entailed automatic excommunication, and banned books favouring Freemasonry.
rewrite: The Roman Catholic Church holds the longest-standing opposition to Freemasonry, primarily objecting to its naturalistic deistic teachings as contradictory to Church doctrine. This stance has been formalized through multiple Papal pronouncements, beginning with Pope Clement XII's *In eminenti apostolatus* in 1738 and extending to Pope Leo XIII's *Ab apostolici* in 1890. The 1917 Code of Canon Law further enforced this position, mandating automatic excommunication for members and prohibiting pro-Masonic literature.

input: Area air defence, the air defence of a specific area or location, (as opposed to point defence), have historically been operated by both armies (Anti-Aircraft Command in the British Army, for instance) and Air Forces (the United States Air Force's CIM-10 Bomarc). Area defence systems have medium to long range and can be made up of various other systems and networked into an area defence system (in which case it may be made up of several short range systems combined to effectively cover an area). An example of area defence is the defence of Saudi Arabia and Israel by MIM-104 Patriot missile batteries during the first Gulf War, where the objective was to cover populated areas.
rewrite: Area air defense protects a specific region, differing from point defense. Historically, both armies and air forces have operated such systems, like the British Army's Anti-Aircraft Command or the U.S. Air Force's CIM-10 Bomarc. These systems typically have medium to long range. They can integrate various other systems into a networked defense, sometimes combining multiple short-range systems to cover a broader area effectively. For example, during the first Gulf War, MIM-104 Patriot missile batteries provided area defense for populated regions in Saudi Arabia and Israel.

input: With roots dating back to 1909 in the university's School of Social Economy, the George Warren Brown School of Social Work (commonly called the Brown School or Brown) was founded in 1925. Brown's academic degree offerings include a Master of Social Work (MSW), a Master of Public Health (MPH), a PhD in Social Work, and a PhD in Public Health Sciences. It is currently ranked first among Master of Social Work programs in the United States. The school was endowed by Bettie Bofinger Brown and named for her husband, George Warren Brown, a St. Louis philanthropist and co-founder of the Brown Shoe Company. The school was the first in the country to have a building for the purpose of social work education, and it is also a founding member of the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health. The school is housed within Brown and Goldfarb Halls, but a third building expansion is currently in progress and slated to be completed in summer 2015. The new building, adjacent to Brown and Goldfarb Halls, targets LEED Gold certification and will add approximately 105,000 square feet, more than doubling the school's teaching, research, and program space.
rewrite:
Founded in 1925, the George Warren Brown School of Social Work—often referred to as the Brown School or simply Brown—traces its origins to 1909 within the university’s School of Social Economy. The school was endowed by Bettie Bofinger Brown and named for her husband, George Warren Brown, a St. Louis philanthropist and co-founder of the Brown Shoe Company. Its academic programs include a Master of Social Work (MSW), a Master of Public Health (MPH), a PhD in Social Work, and a PhD in Public Health Sciences. Currently ranked first among Master of Social Work programs in the United States, the school holds the distinction of being the first in the nation to occupy a building dedicated solely to social work education. It is also a founding member of the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health.

Housed in Brown and Goldfarb Halls, the school is undergoing expansion with a third building, set for completion in summer 2015. This new structure, adjacent to the existing halls, aims for LEED Gold certification. It will add roughly 105,000 square feet, more than doubling the available space for teaching, research, and programs.

input: The oak forests of the southern and central Appalachians consist largely of black, northern red, white, chestnut and scarlet oaks (Quercus velutina, Q. rubra, Q. alba, Q. prinus and Q. coccinea) and hickories, such as the pignut (Carya glabra) in particular. The richest forests, which grade into mesic types, usually in coves and on gentle slopes, have dominantly white and northern red oaks, while the driest sites are dominated by chestnut oak, or sometimes by scarlet or northern red oaks. In the northern Appalachians the oaks, except for white and northern red, drop out, while the latter extends farthest north.
rewrite: In the southern and central Appalachians, oak forests are primarily composed of species like black, northern red, white, chestnut, and scarlet oaks, along with hickories such as the pignut. The most diverse forests, often found in coves and on gentle slopes, transition to mesic types and are dominated by white and northern red oaks. Conversely, the driest areas feature chestnut oak as the main species, sometimes joined by scarlet or northern red oaks. Moving to the northern Appalachians, most oak species disappear, with only the northern red oak extending furthest north.

input: Dominic's search for a close relationship with God was determined and unceasing. He rarely spoke, so little of his interior life is known. What is known about it comes from accounts written by people near to him. St. Cecilia remembered him as cheerful, charitable and full of unceasing vigor. From a number of accounts, singing was apparently one of Dominic's great delights. Dominic practiced self-scourging and would mortify himself as he prayed alone in the chapel at night for 'poor sinners.' He owned a single habit, refused to carry money, and would allow no one to serve him.
rewrite: Dominic's determined, unceasing quest for closeness to God remains largely mysterious, as he spoke little. Insights come from those near him, like St. Cecilia, who recalled his cheer, charity, and relentless vigor. Accounts note singing was a great delight. At night, praying alone for 'poor sinners,' he practiced self-scourging. He owned just one habit, refused money, and would not be served by anyone.

input: In his book, The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution, biologist Richard Dawkins grapples with the question of why pain has to be so very painful. He describes the alternative as a simple, mental raising of a "red flag". To argue why that red flag might be insufficient, Dawkins explains that drives must compete with each other within living beings. The most fit creature would be the one whose pains are well balanced. Those pains which mean certain death when ignored will become the most powerfully felt. The relative intensities of pain, then, may resemble the relative importance of that risk to our ancestors (lack of food, too much cold, or serious injuries are felt as agony, whereas minor damage is felt as mere discomfort). This resemblance will not be perfect, however, because natural selection can be a poor designer. The result is often glitches in animals, including supernormal stimuli. Such glitches help explain pains which are not, or at least no longer directly adaptive (e.g. perhaps some forms of toothache, or injury to fingernails).
rewrite: In *The Greatest Show on Earth: The Evidence for Evolution*, biologist Richard Dawkins explores why pain is so intensely felt. He suggests a simpler alternative could be a mere mental "red flag." Dawkins argues this signal would be inadequate because various drives compete within an organism. The most evolutionarily fit creature is one with a well-calibrated pain system, where the most severe pains correspond to threats that would have meant certain death if ignored. Consequently, the relative intensity of pain likely mirrors the relative historical importance of various dangers to our ancestors. A lack of food, extreme cold, or grave injuries register as agony, while minor damage is only discomfort. This mirroring is imperfect, however, as natural selection is an imperfect designer, often producing glitches. These include supernormal stimuli and help explain pains that are not directly adaptive, such as certain toothaches or injuries to fingernails.

input: On March 27, 1964, the massive Good Friday earthquake killed 133 people and destroyed several villages and portions of large coastal communities, mainly by the resultant tsunamis and landslides. It was the second-most-powerful earthquake in the recorded history of the world, with a moment magnitude of 9.2. It was over one thousand times more powerful than the 1989 San Francisco earthquake. The time of day (5:36 pm), time of year and location of the epicenter were all cited as factors in potentially sparing thousands of lives, particularly in Anchorage.
rewrite: On March 27, 1964, a massive earthquake struck on Good Friday. With a moment magnitude of 9.2, it ranks as the second-most-powerful quake in recorded global history. Its force was over one thousand times greater than the 1989 San Francisco earthquake. The disaster killed 133 people, largely through resulting tsunamis and landslides, which destroyed several villages and parts of major coastal communities. That the epicenter’s location, the time of day (5:36 pm), and the time of year may have spared thousands of lives, especially in Anchorage, was noted.

input: In contrast to the Fed, the ECB normally does not buy bonds outright. The normal procedure used by the ECB for manipulating the money supply has been via the so-called refinancing facilities. In these facilities, bonds are not purchased but used in reverse transactions: repurchase agreements, or collateralised loans. These two transactions are similar, i.e. bonds are used as collaterals for loans, the difference being of legal nature. In the repos the ownership of the collateral changes to the ECB until the loan is repaid.
rewrite: Unlike the Fed, the ECB typically avoids direct bond purchases. Its standard method for adjusting the money supply involves refinancing facilities. Here, bonds are not bought outright but are utilized in reverse transactions like repurchase agreements or collateralized loans. While both involve using bonds as loan collateral and differ mainly in legal terms, repos specifically transfer collateral ownership to the ECB until the loan is repaid.

input: The Shang dynasty oracle bone script and the Zhou dynasty scripts found on Chinese bronze inscriptions are no longer used; the oldest script that is still in use today is the Seal Script (篆書(书), zhuànshū). It evolved organically out of the Spring and Autumn period Zhou script, and was adopted in a standardized form under the first Emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang. The seal script, as the name suggests, is now used only in artistic seals. Few people are still able to read it effortlessly today, although the art of carving a traditional seal in the script remains alive; some calligraphers also work in this style.
rewrite: While the ancient Shang dynasty oracle bone script and Zhou dynasty bronze inscription scripts are obsolete, the oldest surviving form still in use is the Seal Script (篆書(书), zhuànshū). Evolving naturally from the Zhou script of the Spring and Autumn period, it was later standardized under China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang. True to its name, it is now employed almost exclusively for artistic seals. Although few can read it easily today, the craft of carving traditional seals endures, and some calligraphers continue to practice this style.

input: Lasers emitting in the red region of the spectrum have been available since the invention of the ruby laser in 1960. In 1962 the red helium–neon laser was invented, and these two types of lasers were widely used in many scientific applications including holography, and in education. Red helium–neon lasers were used commercially in LaserDisc players. The use of red laser diodes became widespread with the commercial success of modern DVD players, which use a 660 nm laser diode technology. Today, red and red-orange laser diodes are widely available to the public in the form of extremely inexpensive laser pointers. Portable, high-powered versions are also available for various applications. More recently, 671 nm diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) lasers have been introduced to the market for all-DPSS laser display systems, particle image velocimetry, Raman spectroscopy, and holography.
rewrite: Since the ruby laser's 1960 introduction, red-spectrum lasers have been accessible. Following this, the 1962 invention of the red helium-neon laser saw both types become common in scientific and educational roles, such as holography. Commercially, red helium-neon lasers were employed in LaserDisc players. Widespread adoption of red laser diodes, however, came with modern DVD players using 660 nm diode technology. Presently, the public can easily obtain inexpensive red and red-orange laser pointers, alongside portable, high-powered models for diverse uses. Most recently, 671 nm diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) lasers have entered the market, serving applications in all-DPSS laser displays, particle image velocimetry, Raman spectroscopy, and holography.

input: Cities not served by road, sea, or river can be reached only by air, foot, dogsled, or snowmachine, accounting for Alaska's extremely well developed bush air services—an Alaskan novelty. Anchorage and, to a lesser extent Fairbanks, is served by many major airlines. Because of limited highway access, air travel remains the most efficient form of transportation in and out of the state. Anchorage recently completed extensive remodeling and construction at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport to help accommodate the upsurge in tourism (in 2012-2013, Alaska received almost 2 million visitors).
rewrite: Alaska's limited road, sea, and river access to many cities makes air, foot, dogsled, or snowmachine the only options, leading to a highly developed bush air service—a unique feature of the state. Air travel is the most efficient transportation into and out of Alaska due to sparse highways. Major airlines primarily serve Anchorage, and to a lesser degree, Fairbanks. To handle a tourism surge of nearly 2 million visitors in 2012-2013, Anchorage recently finished major remodeling and construction at Ted Stevens International Airport.

input: The islands enjoy a mild climate and varied soils, giving rise to a diverse pattern of vegetation. Animal and plant life is similar to that of the northwestern European continent. There are however, fewer numbers of species, with Ireland having even less. All native flora and fauna in Ireland is made up of species that migrated from elsewhere in Europe, and Great Britain in particular. The only window when this could have occurred was between the end of the last Ice Age (about 12,000 years ago) and when the land bridge connecting the two islands was flooded by sea (about 8,000 years ago).
rewrite: With a mild climate and varied soils, the islands support diverse vegetation. Their animal and plant life resembles that of northwestern Europe, though with fewer species overall; Ireland has the fewest. All native Irish flora and fauna consist of species that migrated from Europe, primarily Great Britain. This migration could only have happened within a specific window: after the last Ice Age ended roughly 12,000 years ago and before the connecting land bridge was flooded by the sea around 8,000 years ago.

input: Full-featured USB Type-C cables are active, electronically marked cables that contain a chip with an ID function based on the configuration data channel and vendor-defined messages (VDMs) from the USB Power Delivery 2.0 specification. USB Type-C devices also support power currents of 1.5 A and 3.0 A over the 5 V power bus in addition to baseline 900 mA; devices can either negotiate increased USB current through the configuration line, or they can support the full Power Delivery specification using both BMC-coded configuration line and legacy BFSK-coded VBUS line.
rewrite: Active, electronically marked USB Type-C cables are full-featured and incorporate a chip. This chip uses the configuration data channel and VDMs from the USB Power Delivery 2.0 specification for identification. Beyond the baseline 900 mA, these devices support 1.5 A and 3.0 A currents over the 5 V bus. To manage higher power, they can negotiate increased current via the configuration line or fully adopt the Power Delivery specification, utilizing both the BMC-coded configuration line and the legacy BFSK-coded VBUS line.

input: AA gunnery was a difficult business. The problem was of successfully aiming a shell to burst close to its target's future position, with various factors affecting the shells' predicted trajectory. This was called deflection gun-laying, 'off-set' angles for range and elevation were set on the gunsight and updated as their target moved. In this method when the sights were on the target, the barrel was pointed at the target's future position. Range and height of the target determined fuse length. The difficulties increased as aircraft performance improved.
rewrite: Accurately aiming anti-aircraft guns was a complex challenge, known as deflection gun-laying. It required calculating precise 'off-set' angles for range and elevation on the gunsight, constantly updated as the target moved. The goal was to fire a shell to burst where the aircraft would be, not where it was, accounting for factors affecting the shell's path. When the sights aligned on the target, the barrel actually aimed ahead at its future position, with fuse length set by the target's range and height. These difficulties only grew as aircraft became more advanced.

input: From the 18th century through late 20th century, the history of science, especially of the physical and biological sciences, was often presented in a progressive narrative in which true theories replaced false beliefs. More recent historical interpretations, such as those of Thomas Kuhn, tend to portray the history of science in different terms, such as that of competing paradigms or conceptual systems in a wider matrix that includes intellectual, cultural, economic and political themes outside of science.
rewrite: From the 18th to the late 20th century, the history of science—particularly in physics and biology—was frequently told as a story of progress, with true theories displacing false beliefs. More recent interpretations, like those of Thomas Kuhn, depict it differently. They frame it as a history of competing paradigms or conceptual systems, situated within a broader matrix of intellectual, cultural, economic, and political themes.

input: Active solar techniques use photovoltaics, concentrated solar power, solar thermal collectors, pumps, and fans to convert sunlight into useful outputs. Passive solar techniques include selecting materials with favorable thermal properties, designing spaces that naturally circulate air, and referencing the position of a building to the Sun. Active solar technologies increase the supply of energy and are considered supply side technologies, while passive solar technologies reduce the need for alternate resources and are generally considered demand side technologies.
rewrite: Active solar methods employ photovoltaics, concentrated solar power, collectors, pumps, and fans to transform sunlight into practical outputs. In contrast, passive techniques involve choosing materials with beneficial thermal properties, designing for natural air circulation, and orienting buildings relative to the Sun. While active technologies boost energy supply and are seen as supply-side solutions, passive approaches lower the demand for alternative resources, typically classifying them as demand-side technologies.

input: The ownership of the Spectre organisation—originally stylised "SPECTRE" as an acronym of SPecial Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge and Extortion—and its characters, had been at the centre of long-standing litigation starting in 1961 between Ian Fleming and Kevin McClory over the film rights to the novel Thunderball. The dispute began after Fleming incorporated elements of an undeveloped film script written by McClory and screenwriter Jack Whittingham—including characters and plot points—into Thunderball, which McClory contested in court, claiming ownership over elements of the novel. In 1963, Fleming settled out of court with McClory, in an agreement which awarded McClory the film rights. This enabled him to become a producer for the 1965 film Thunderball—with Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman as executive producers—and the non-Eon film Never Say Never Again, an updated remake of Thunderball, in 1983.[N 3] A second remake, entitled Warhead 2000 A.D., was planned for production and release in the 1990s before being abandoned. Under the terms of the 1963 settlement, the literary rights stayed with Fleming, allowing the Spectre organisation and associated characters to continue appearing in print.
rewrite: The long-standing legal dispute over the ownership of the Spectre organisation—originally styled as the acronym "SPECTRE" for SPecial Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge and Extortion—and its characters began in 1961. Ian Fleming and Kevin McClory were in conflict over the film rights to the novel *Thunderball*. Fleming had incorporated material from an undeveloped film script by McClory and screenwriter Jack Whittingham, including characters and plot elements, into the book. McClory challenged this in court, asserting his ownership over these aspects. A 1963 out-of-court settlement granted McClory the film rights. Consequently, he served as a producer for the 1965 film *Thunderball*, which had Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman as executive producers, and later for the 1983 non-Eon remake *Never Say Never Again*. A planned second remake, *Warhead 2000 A.D.*, was abandoned in the 1990s. However, the literary rights remained with Fleming per the settlement, permitting Spectre and its characters to continue in print.

input: The quarrel of the Ancients and the Moderns was a literary and artistic quarrel that heated up in the early 1690s and shook the Académie française. The opposing two sides were, the Ancients (Anciens) who constrain choice of subjects to those drawn from the literature of Antiquity and the Moderns (Modernes), who supported the merits of the authors of the century of Louis XIV. Fontenelle quickly followed with his Digression sur les anciens et les modernes (1688), in which he took the Modern side, pressing the argument that modern scholarship allowed modern man to surpass the ancients in knowledge.
rewrite: Heating up in the early 1690s, the quarrel of the Ancients and the Moderns shook the Académie française. This literary and artistic debate pitted two sides against each other. The Ancients (Anciens) constrained subject choice to themes from Antiquity's literature, while the Moderns (Modernes) championed the merits of authors from the century of Louis XIV. Taking the Modern side, Fontenelle pressed his argument in his *Digression sur les anciens et les modernes* (1688). He contended that modern scholarship enabled contemporary man to surpass the ancients in knowledge.

input: Complex serological techniques have been developed into what are known as Immunoassays. Immunoassays can use the basic antibody – antigen binding as the basis to produce an electro - magnetic or particle radiation signal, which can be detected by some form of instrumentation. Signal of unknowns can be compared to that of standards allowing quantitation of the target antigen. To aid in the diagnosis of infectious diseases, immunoassays can detect or measure antigens from either infectious agents or proteins generated by an infected organism in response to a foreign agent. For example, immunoassay A may detect the presence of a surface protein from a virus particle. Immunoassay B on the other hand may detect or measure antibodies produced by an organism's immune system that are made to neutralize and allow the destruction of the virus.
rewrite: Immunoassays are advanced serological methods built upon fundamental antibody-antigen binding. This interaction generates a measurable electromagnetic or particle radiation signal, detected through specialized instrumentation. By comparing signals from unknown samples to established standards, these assays enable precise quantitation of target antigens. In infectious disease diagnostics, immunoassays are invaluable for identifying antigens from pathogens or detecting proteins produced by the host in response to infection. For instance, one type of immunoassay might identify a specific viral surface protein. Conversely, another could measure the antibodies created by the immune system to neutralize and eliminate the virus.

input: The earliest known chemical evidence of barley beer dates to circa 3500–3100 BC from the site of Godin Tepe in the Zagros Mountains of western Iran. Some of the earliest Sumerian writings contain references to beer; examples include a prayer to the goddess Ninkasi, known as "The Hymn to Ninkasi", which served as both a prayer as well as a method of remembering the recipe for beer in a culture with few literate people, and the ancient advice (Fill your belly. Day and night make merry) to Gilgamesh, recorded in the Epic of Gilgamesh, by the ale-wife Siduri may, at least in part, have referred to the consumption of beer. The Ebla tablets, discovered in 1974 in Ebla, Syria, show that beer was produced in the city in 2500 BC. A fermented beverage using rice and fruit was made in China around 7000 BC. Unlike sake, mould was not used to saccharify the rice (amylolytic fermentation); the rice was probably prepared for fermentation by mastication or malting.
rewrite: Evidence of barley beer from approximately 3500–3100 BC, identified through chemical analysis, comes from Godin Tepe in western Iran's Zagros Mountains. In early Sumerian writings, beer is referenced in works such as "The Hymn to Ninkasi," a prayer to the goddess that also functioned as a memorable recipe in a largely non-literate society. Further Sumerian mention appears in the Epic of Gilgamesh, where the ale-wife Siduri’s advice to "Fill your belly. Day and night make merry" likely alludes to beer consumption. Production is also documented around 2500 BC in Ebla, Syria, as shown by tablets unearthed in 1974. Separately, a fermented drink made from rice and fruit was being produced in China as early as 7000 BC. Here, the rice was likely prepared for fermentation through chewing or malting, not by using mould for saccharification as in sake, representing a distinct amylolytic process.

input: The Governor of Michigan, Rick Snyder, declared a financial emergency for the city in March 2013, appointing an emergency manager. On July 18, 2013, Detroit filed the largest municipal bankruptcy case in U.S. history. It was declared bankrupt by Judge Steven W. Rhodes of the Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan on December 3, 2013; he cited its $18.5 billion debt and declared that negotiations with its thousands of creditors were unfeasible. On November 7, 2014, Judge Rhodes approved the city's bankruptcy plan, allowing the city to begin the process of exiting bankruptcy. The City of Detroit successfully exited Chapter 9 municipal bankruptcy with all finances handed back to the city at midnight on December 11, 2014.
rewrite: In March 2013, Michigan Governor Rick Snyder declared a financial emergency for Detroit and appointed an emergency manager. The city then filed the largest municipal bankruptcy case in U.S. history on July 18, 2013. That December, Judge Steven W. Rhodes of the Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan declared Detroit bankrupt, citing its $18.5 billion debt and deeming negotiations with its many creditors unfeasible. Approval of the city’s bankruptcy plan followed on November 7, 2014, permitting Detroit to start exiting bankruptcy. Finally, at midnight on December 11, 2014, the City of Detroit successfully exited Chapter 9 bankruptcy, with full financial control returned to the city.

input: DST's potential to save energy comes primarily from its effects on residential lighting, which consumes about 3.5% of electricity in the United States and Canada. Delaying the nominal time of sunset and sunrise reduces the use of artificial light in the evening and increases it in the morning. As Franklin's 1784 satire pointed out, lighting costs are reduced if the evening reduction outweighs the morning increase, as in high-latitude summer when most people wake up well after sunrise. An early goal of DST was to reduce evening usage of incandescent lighting, which used to be a primary use of electricity. Although energy conservation remains an important goal, energy usage patterns have greatly changed since then, and recent research is limited and reports contradictory results. Electricity use is greatly affected by geography, climate, and economics, making it hard to generalize from single studies.
rewrite: The primary energy-saving potential of Daylight Saving Time (DST) lies in altering residential lighting patterns, which account for roughly 3.5% of electricity use in the United States and Canada. By shifting the nominal times of sunset and sunrise, artificial light use decreases in the evening but rises in the morning. As noted in Benjamin Franklin's 1784 satire, net savings occur if the evening reduction exceeds the morning increase—a scenario typical in high-latitude summers, when many wake after sunrise. Originally, a key objective was to cut evening consumption of incandescent lighting, once a major electrical load. While conservation remains a goal, energy use patterns have shifted dramatically. Recent studies are limited and show conflicting outcomes, partly because geography, climate, and economics heavily influence electricity consumption, complicating generalizations from individual research.

input: The Executive Board is responsible for the implementation of monetary policy (defined by the Governing Council) and the day-to-day running of the bank. It can issue decisions to national central banks and may also exercise powers delegated to it by the Governing Council. It is composed of the President of the Bank (currently Mario Draghi), the Vice-President (currently Vitor Constâncio) and four other members. They are all appointed for non-renewable terms of eight years. They are appointed "from among persons of recognised standing and professional experience in monetary or banking matters by common accord of the governments of the Member States at the level of Heads of State or Government, on a recommendation from the Council, after it has consulted the European Parliament and the Governing Council of the ECB". The Executive Board normally meets every Tuesday.
rewrite: Composed of the President (currently Mario Draghi), the Vice-President (Vitor Constâncio), and four other members, the Executive Board handles the bank’s daily operations and implements monetary policy as defined by the Governing Council. Its members are appointed for single, non-renewable eight-year terms. Selection requires common accord among EU governments at the level of Heads of State or Government, based on a Council recommendation and following consultations with the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council. Candidates must possess recognized standing and professional experience in monetary or banking matters. In its regular Tuesday meetings, the Board can issue decisions to national central banks and may also exercise any powers delegated by the Governing Council.

input: Less than 1% of all species that have been described have been studied beyond simply noting their existence. The vast majority of Earth's species are microbial. Contemporary biodiversity physics is "firmly fixated on the visible [macroscopic] world". For example, microbial life is metabolically and environmentally more diverse than multicellular life (see e.g., extremophile). "On the tree of life, based on analyses of small-subunit ribosomal RNA, visible life consists of barely noticeable twigs. The inverse relationship of size and population recurs higher on the evolutionary ladder—"to a first approximation, all multicellular species on Earth are insects". Insect extinction rates are high—supporting the Holocene extinction hypothesis.
rewrite: Current understanding of biodiversity remains heavily focused on the macroscopic world, yet the vast majority of Earth's species are microbial. Remarkably, less than 1% of all described species have been studied beyond their initial documentation. Microbial life displays far greater metabolic and environmental diversity than multicellular organisms, as seen in extremophiles. On the tree of life, visible multicellular life forms mere twigs. Furthermore, an inverse relationship between size and population scale persists, meaning that, to a first approximation, all multicellular species are insects. Their high extinction rates lend support to the Holocene extinction hypothesis.

input: Apple discontinued the use of PowerPC microprocessors in 2006. At WWDC 2005, Steve Jobs announced this transition, revealing that Mac OS X was always developed to run on both the Intel and PowerPC architectures. All new Macs now use x86 processors made by Intel, and some were renamed as a result. Intel-based Macs running OS X 10.6 and below (support has been discontinued since 10.7) can run pre-existing software developed for PowerPC using an emulator called Rosetta, although at noticeably slower speeds than native programs. However, the Classic environment is unavailable on the Intel architecture. Intel chips introduced the potential to run the Microsoft Windows operating system natively on Apple hardware, without emulation software such as Virtual PC. In March 2006, a group of hackers announced that they were able to run Windows XP on an Intel-based Mac. The group released their software as open source and has posted it for download on their website. On April 5, 2006, Apple announced the availability of the public beta of Boot Camp, software that allows owners of Intel-based Macs to install Windows XP on their machines; later versions added support for Windows Vista and Windows 7. Classic was discontinued in Mac OS X 10.5, and Boot Camp became a standard feature on Intel-based Macs.
rewrite:
In 2006, Apple ceased using PowerPC microprocessors, a transition Steve Jobs had announced at WWDC the previous year. He revealed that Mac OS X had always been designed to function on both Intel and PowerPC architectures. Consequently, all new Macs began utilizing Intel’s x86 processors, with some models even being renamed. For software originally developed for PowerPC, Intel-based Macs running OS X 10.6 or earlier—support ended with 10.7—could employ the Rosetta emulator, though performance was notably slower than with native programs. Notably, the Classic environment remained unavailable on the Intel platform.

This architectural shift unlocked the potential to run Microsoft Windows natively on Apple hardware, eliminating the need for emulation tools like Virtual PC. By March 2006, a group of hackers demonstrated this capability by running Windows XP on an Intel Mac, releasing their open-source software for download. Shortly after, on April 5, 2006, Apple launched the public beta of Boot Camp, enabling Intel Mac owners to install Windows XP; later updates extended support to Windows Vista and Windows 7. While the Classic environment was discontinued in Mac OS X 10.5, Boot Camp became a standard feature on all Intel-based Macs.

input: The language of the Quran has been described as "rhymed prose" as it partakes of both poetry and prose; however, this description runs the risk of failing to convey the rhythmic quality of Quranic language, which is more poetic in some parts and more prose-like in others. Rhyme, while found throughout the Quran, is conspicuous in many of the earlier Meccan suras, in which relatively short verses throw the rhyming words into prominence. The effectiveness of such a form is evident for instance in Sura 81, and there can be no doubt that these passages impressed the conscience of the hearers. Frequently a change of rhyme from one set of verses to another signals a change in the subject of discussion. Later sections also preserve this form but the style is more expository.
rewrite: The Quran's language is often called "rhymed prose," blending elements of poetry and prose, yet this term may not fully capture its rhythmic nature, which varies from highly poetic to more prosaic sections. Rhyme is a consistent feature, particularly prominent in the earlier Meccan suras. There, shorter verses emphasize the rhyming words, as seen in Sura 81, undoubtedly leaving a strong impression on listeners. Shifts in rhyme frequently indicate a change in topic. While later sections maintain this form, their style becomes more explanatory.

input: Montana's personal income tax contains 7 brackets, with rates ranging from 1 percent to 6.9 percent. Montana has no sales tax. In Montana, household goods are exempt from property taxes. However, property taxes are assessed on livestock, farm machinery, heavy equipment, automobiles, trucks, and business equipment. The amount of property tax owed is not determined solely by the property's value. The property's value is multiplied by a tax rate, set by the Montana Legislature, to determine its taxable value. The taxable value is then multiplied by the mill levy established by various taxing jurisdictions—city and county government, school districts and others.
rewrite: Montana imposes no sales tax, and household goods are exempt from property taxes. The state's personal income tax features seven brackets, with rates from 1% to 6.9%. Property taxes do apply to items like livestock, farm machinery, heavy equipment, vehicles, and business equipment. The tax owed is not based on property value alone. First, the property's value is multiplied by a legislatively set tax rate to find its taxable value. This taxable value is then multiplied by the mill levy, which is established by local taxing jurisdictions such as city and county governments and school districts.

input: Encouraged by these successes, Nintendo soon turned its attention to the North American market. Nintendo entered into negotiations with Atari to release the Famicom under Atari’s name as the name Nintendo Advanced Video Gaming System. The deal was set to be finalized and signed at the Summer Consumer Electronics Show in June 1983. However, Atari discovered at that show that its competitor Coleco was illegally demonstrating its Coleco Adam computer with Nintendo's Donkey Kong game. This violation of Atari's exclusive license with Nintendo to publish the game for its own computer systems delayed the implementation of Nintendo's game console marketing contract with Atari. Atari's CEO Ray Kassar was fired the next month, so the deal went nowhere, and Nintendo decided to market its system on its own.g[›]
rewrite: Nintendo, buoyed by its prior successes, next aimed to enter the North American market. To do so, it negotiated with Atari to release the Famicom console under the name Nintendo Advanced Video Gaming System. The agreement was poised for finalization at the Summer Consumer Electronics Show in June 1983. There, however, Atari learned that its rival Coleco was unlawfully demonstrating the Coleco Adam computer using Nintendo's Donkey Kong game. This breached Atari's exclusive license to publish the game for its computers, which in turn stalled the broader console marketing contract with Nintendo. Following the firing of Atari's CEO Ray Kassar the next month, the deal collapsed entirely. Consequently, Nintendo chose to market the system independently.

input: The two neurotransmitters that are used most widely in the vertebrate brain are glutamate, which almost always exerts excitatory effects on target neurons, and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), which is almost always inhibitory. Neurons using these transmitters can be found in nearly every part of the brain. Because of their ubiquity, drugs that act on glutamate or GABA tend to have broad and powerful effects. Some general anesthetics act by reducing the effects of glutamate; most tranquilizers exert their sedative effects by enhancing the effects of GABA.
rewrite: Glutamate and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) are the most widely used neurotransmitters in the vertebrate brain. Glutamate is nearly always excitatory, while GABA is almost always inhibitory. Neurons employing these transmitters are present in nearly every brain region. Consequently, drugs targeting glutamate or GABA typically produce broad and powerful effects. For instance, some general anesthetics work by diminishing glutamate's effects, whereas many tranquilizers enhance GABA's activity to produce sedation.

input: Research suggests that sexual orientation is independent of cultural and other social influences, but that open identification of one's sexual orientation may be hindered by homophobic/hetereosexist settings. Social systems such as religion, language and ethnic traditions can have a powerful impact on realization of sexual orientation. Influences of culture may complicate the process of measuring sexual orientation. The majority of empirical and clinical research on LGBT populations are done with largely white, middle-class, well-educated samples, however there are pockets of research that document various other cultural groups, although these are frequently limited in diversity of gender and sexual orientation of the subjects. Integration of sexual orientation with sociocultural identity may be a challenge for LGBT individuals. Individuals may or may not consider their sexual orientation to define their sexual identity, as they may experience various degrees of fluidity of sexuality, or may simply identify more strongly with another aspect of their identity such as family role. American culture puts a great emphasis on individual attributes, and views the self as unchangeable and constant. In contrast, East Asian cultures put a great emphasis on a person's social role within social hierarchies, and view the self as fluid and malleable. These differing cultural perspectives have many implications on cognitions of the self, including perception of sexual orientation.
rewrite: Research indicates that while sexual orientation itself is not shaped by cultural or social factors, the willingness to openly identify with it can be suppressed in homophobic or heterosexist environments. Systems like religion, language, and ethnic traditions exert a strong influence on how one comes to understand their own orientation. This cultural dimension also complicates attempts to measure sexual orientation. Much empirical and clinical study of LGBT communities relies on samples that are predominantly white, middle-class, and well-educated. Although some research does cover other cultural groups, it often lacks diversity in the genders and sexual orientations represented among subjects. For LGBT individuals, integrating sexual orientation with their broader sociocultural identity can be difficult. Some may see their orientation as central to their identity, while others, experiencing sexuality with fluidity, might prioritize different aspects of themselves, such as a family role. Cultural perspectives on identity vary widely. American culture, for instance, emphasizes individual, stable traits, viewing the self as fixed. Conversely, East Asian cultures place greater importance on social roles within hierarchies, seeing the self as adaptable. These contrasting views significantly affect how the self is understood, including the perception of one’s sexual orientation.

input: Research has generally shown striking uniformity across different cultures in the motives behind teen alcohol use. Social engagement and personal enjoyment appear to play a fairly universal role in adolescents' decision to drink throughout separate cultural contexts. Surveys conducted in Argentina, Hong Kong, and Canada have each indicated the most common reason for drinking among adolescents to relate to pleasure and recreation; 80% of Argentinian teens reported drinking for enjoyment, while only 7% drank to improve a bad mood. The most prevalent answers among Canadian adolescents were to "get in a party mood," 18%; "because I enjoy it," 16%; and "to get drunk," 10%. In Hong Kong, female participants most frequently reported drinking for social enjoyment, while males most frequently reported drinking to feel the effects of alcohol.
rewrite: Studies across diverse cultures reveal a consistent pattern in why adolescents consume alcohol, with social engagement and personal enjoyment being universally prominent motives. Surveys from Argentina, Hong Kong, and Canada illustrate this commonality. In Argentina, 80% of teens cited drinking for enjoyment, compared to just 7% who drank to improve a bad mood. Canadian adolescents most frequently reported motives like getting in a party mood (18%), personal enjoyment (16%), and getting drunk (10%). Similarly, in Hong Kong, social enjoyment was the top reason for female participants, while males most often drank to feel the effects of alcohol. This cross-cultural research highlights a striking uniformity in the recreational and social drivers behind teen drinking.

input: Aristotle's explanation of how this was possible was not strictly empiricist in a modern sense, but rather based on his theory of potentiality and actuality, and experience of sense perceptions still requires the help of the active nous. These notions contrasted with Platonic notions of the human mind as an entity that pre-existed somewhere in the heavens, before being sent down to join a body on Earth (see Plato's Phaedo and Apology, as well as others). Aristotle was considered to give a more important position to sense perception than Plato, and commentators in the Middle Ages summarized one of his positions as "nihil in intellectu nisi prius fuerit in sensu" (Latin for "nothing in the intellect without first being in the senses").
rewrite: Aristotle’s account of this process was not empiricist in the modern sense. Instead, it relied on his concepts of potentiality and actuality, and he held that even sense perception requires the active intellect, or nous. This stood in contrast to Plato’s view, found in works like the *Phaedo* and *Apology*, which described the mind as a pre-existing heavenly entity later joined with a body. Aristotle placed greater emphasis on sensory experience than Plato did. Medieval commentators later encapsulated one key Aristotelian stance in the Latin maxim: “nihil in intellectu nisi prius fuerit in sensu”—nothing is in the intellect that was not first in the senses.

input: Since over half of GE's revenue is derived from financial services, it is arguably a financial company with a manufacturing arm. It is also one of the largest lenders in countries other than the United States, such as Japan. Even though the first wave of conglomerates (such as ITT Corporation, Ling-Temco-Vought, Tenneco, etc.) fell by the wayside by the mid-1980s, in the late 1990s, another wave (consisting of Westinghouse, Tyco, and others) tried and failed to emulate GE's success.[citation needed]

It ranks among the top lenders in nations like Japan, outside the U.S. Although early conglomerates like ITT faded by the 1980s, a later wave in the 1990s, including Westinghouse and Tyco, attempted to replicate GE's model without success.

input: The Miami area has a unique dialect, (commonly called the "Miami accent") which is widely spoken. The dialect developed among second- or third-generation Hispanics, including Cuban-Americans, whose first language was English (though some non-Hispanic white, black, and other races who were born and raised the Miami area tend to adopt it as well.) It is based on a fairly standard American accent but with some changes very similar to dialects in the Mid-Atlantic (especially the New York area dialect, Northern New Jersey English, and New York Latino English.) Unlike Virginia Piedmont, Coastal Southern American, and Northeast American dialects and Florida Cracker dialect (see section below), "Miami accent" is rhotic; it also incorporates a rhythm and pronunciation heavily influenced by Spanish (wherein rhythm is syllable-timed). However, this is a native dialect of English, not learner English or interlanguage; it is possible to differentiate this variety from an interlanguage spoken by second-language speakers in that "Miami accent" does not generally display the following features: there is no addition of /ɛ/ before initial consonant clusters with /s/, speakers do not confuse of /dʒ/ with /j/, (e.g., Yale with jail), and /r/ and /rr/ are pronounced as alveolar approximant [ɹ] instead of alveolar tap [ɾ] or alveolar trill [r] in Spanish.
rewrite: Widely spoken in the region, the distinctive "Miami accent" is a unique local dialect. It emerged primarily among second- or third-generation Hispanic residents, such as Cuban-Americans, who grew up speaking English as their first language. The accent also finds adoption among many non-Hispanic white, black, and other individuals born and raised in Miami. Rooted in a relatively standard American accent, it incorporates modifications bearing strong similarity to certain Mid-Atlantic dialects, including those of New York City, Northern New Jersey, and New York Latino English. Notably rhotic, it contrasts with various non-rhotic dialects like Virginia Piedmont, Coastal Southern, and traditional Florida Cracker speech. A defining characteristic is its Spanish-influenced, syllable-timed rhythm and pronunciation. Crucially, this is a native English dialect, distinct from the interlanguage of learners. Key differentiators include the absence of an /ɛ/ sound before initial /s/ clusters, no confusion between /dʒ/ (as in "jail") and /j/ (as in "Yale"), and the use of the alveolar approximant [ɹ] for /r/ and /rr/ sounds instead of the Spanish tap [ɾ] or trill [r].

input: Notable exceptions include the massacre of Jews and forcible conversion of some Jews by the rulers of the Almohad dynasty in Al-Andalus in the 12th century, as well as in Islamic Persia, and the forced confinement of Moroccan Jews to walled quarters known as mellahs beginning from the 15th century and especially in the early 19th century. In modern times, it has become commonplace for standard antisemitic themes to be conflated with anti-Zionist publications and pronouncements of Islamic movements such as Hezbollah and Hamas, in the pronouncements of various agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and even in the newspapers and other publications of Turkish Refah Partisi."

This is evident in the publications and pronouncements of Islamic movements like Hezbollah and Hamas, as well as in various agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
